class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Write a script for this repository that tells me what changed in Muse Code since the version I run. Read the installed version from `muse --version`, fetch https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/changelog.md, parse it into releases with their New, Improvements, Fixes and Performance sections, and print every change newer than mine, security fixes first. Exit nonzero when the fetch or the parse fails.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Changelog&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/changelog.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/changelog

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- Each release is a `## &lt;version&gt;` heading, newest first, with `### New`, `### Improvements`, `### Fixes` and `### Performance` sections of `- ` bullets.
- Some releases (1.0.x, 0.1.x) are one paragraph of patch notes instead of sections, and 0.1.0 is a single bullet.
- x in a heading (1.0.x) matches any number. Stop at the first heading at or below the installed version: 1.0.3 stops at 1.0.x, and a version newer than the page has nothing to print.
- Security fixes start with `**Security:**`.
- The page gives no release dates. Its anchors are v plus the version with dots as hyphens (#v1-4-13).

Starter code (Python)
import re
import subprocess
import sys

import requests

out = subprocess.run([&quot;muse&quot;, &quot;--version&quot;], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
found = re.search(r&quot;\d+\.\d+\.\d+&quot;, out)
if not found:
    sys.exit(f&quot;Can&#x27;t read a version from {out!r}&quot;)
mine = [int(n) for n in found.group(0).split(&quot;.&quot;)]

def at_or_below(heading):
    &quot;&quot;&quot;The installed version or older; x matches any number (1.0.x).&quot;&quot;&quot;
    for part, own in zip(heading.split(&quot;.&quot;), mine):
        if part == &quot;x&quot;:
            return True
        if int(part) != own:
            return int(part) &lt; own
    return True

md = requests.get(&quot;https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/changelog.md&quot;, timeout=30)
md.raise_for_status()

changes, version, kind, releases = [], None, &quot;Notes&quot;, 0
for line in md.text.splitlines():
    if line.startswith(&quot;## &quot;):
        releases += 1
        heading = line[3:].split()[0]
        if at_or_below(heading):
            break
        version, kind = heading, &quot;Notes&quot;
    elif version and line.startswith(&quot;### &quot;):
        kind = line[4:].strip()
    elif version and line.strip():
        changes.append((version, kind, line.removeprefix(&quot;- &quot;).strip()))
if not releases:
    sys.exit(&quot;No releases found: has the page&#x27;s format changed?&quot;)
if not changes:
    print(f&quot;Up to date: nothing newer than {found.group(0)}.&quot;)
for v, k, text in sorted(changes, key=lambda c: not c[2].startswith(&quot;**Security&quot;)):
    print(f&quot;{v} [{k}] {text}&quot;)

Done when
- Given 1.4.10 it prints the 1.4.11, 1.4.12 and 1.4.13 changes and nothing older; given 1.0.3 it stops at 1.0.x; given 1.4.14 it says it&#x27;s up to date.
- Security fixes come first, and an unreachable URL exits nonzero.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">3,606<!-- --> For install and upgrade steps, see the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code">Muse Code overview</a>.</p><h2 id="v1-4-13" class="docs-h docs-h2">1.4.13<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v1-4-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><h3 id="new" class="docs-h docs-h3">New<a class="docs-anchor" href="#new" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>On macOS and Linux, permission profiles extending <code class="docs-code-inline">:ask-me</code> with filesystem <code class="docs-code-inline">deny</code> rules now enforce them: workspace-root deny globs (<code class="docs-code-inline">**/*.pem</code>) and absolute/<code class="docs-code-inline">~/</code> denies refuse matching reads and writes, and sandboxed shell access to matching paths that exist when each shell command starts (files created mid-command under a deny glob are not covered on Linux, macOS enforces globs live through Seatbelt regex with no snapshot window; a deny on a not-yet-existing path is masked at its first missing component), instead of being silently ignored, while the profile keeps its write grants elsewhere</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse usage</code> shows your subscription allowance (window and weekly use, reset times, tier) without running a model turn; <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec --json</code> reads it too when the run saw no usage update</span></li><li><span>Desktop and other connected clients offer the same third-party models as the terminal model picker</span></li><li><span>Added a built-in <code class="docs-code-inline">visual-coding</code> skill: for a 3D page, a browser game or Blender work, it points the agent to the one built-in skill that owns that kind of work before any code is written, so one request no longer runs two competing build processes</span></li><li><span>Warnings near your usage limit show the remaining allowance and reset time above the message queue</span></li></ul><h3 id="improvements" class="docs-h docs-h3">Improvements<a class="docs-anchor" href="#improvements" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/game-3d-visuals</code> now runs its plan, build and review as three steps and posts a one-line result to the todo list after each</span></li><li><span>When cleanup after a finished turn keeps failing (goal accounting or the live turn state), the chat now shows one &quot;cleanup failed after this turn&quot; warning naming what gave up, instead of failing silently. It shows right after that turn, or the next time you open the chat if you have already moved on to another turn (in the rare case that the warning itself could not be saved, it shows only while you are still on that turn)</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">--yolo</code> keeps the <code class="docs-code-inline">request_user_input</code> question tool and enables async questions instead of withholding them; pass <code class="docs-code-inline">--disable-request-user-input</code> for runs that should ask nothing</span></li></ul><h3 id="fixes" class="docs-h docs-h3">Fixes<a class="docs-anchor" href="#fixes" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Sessions in untrusted workspaces no longer receive project rules recorded by an earlier trusted session</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Session worktree recovery now enforces the same protected paths as the rest of the session</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Served sessions in workspaces you have not trusted no longer run workspace status checks or Sapling snapshots, and sessions that never establish trust now fail closed instead of inheriting trusted behavior</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> When <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> resumes, forks or opens a side chat from a chat whose saved history lost a permission change, the chat no longer reopens with older, wider permissions: it resets to your defaults, keeps your saved settings when they were stricter, or switches to read-only when the two cannot be safely combined, and &quot;allow for this session&quot; approvals given before the loss stop applying. A permission profile you choose when resuming such a chat applies after the reset, or in its place when the reset is not allowed. When no safe reset exists, or managed policy forbids it, the chat refuses and asks you to start a new chat</span></li><li><span>A chat whose tool result could not be saved (for example on a full disk) can compact again right away, and after a restart that turn is kept with the result shown as lost, instead of disappearing</span></li><li><span>Notes sent to a subagent over a remote session keep their plain summary</span></li><li><span>Removing a queued message with <code class="docs-code-inline">turn/unqueue</code> now works when the message is waiting behind an internal turn, instead of failing with <code class="docs-code-inline">missing_run</code> and running the message anyway</span></li><li><span>Session names you gave earlier show up again in the session list and work with <code class="docs-code-inline">muse resume &lt;name&gt;</code>, read from each session&#x27;s own history</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/feedback</code> uploads with a very large session record no longer fail; the record is shortened to fit and the shortening is noted</span></li><li><span>When a chat&#x27;s file could not be read while loading it for a save (a brief I/O error), the chat goes back to saving its progress once the read works again, instead of staying unable to save until restart</span></li><li><span>Stopping messages say whether a workflow or a background command was stopped</span></li><li><span>Long <code class="docs-code-inline">/goal</code> sessions save their resume checkpoints again, so they stay compact and resume quickly instead of slowing down after every compaction</span></li><li><span>A forked chat where the start of one of its own turns could not be written to disk keeps working after it compacts and is reopened; that turn stays left out, and Muse says so once per reopen</span></li><li><span>A chat that messaged a subagent and then ran several tools at once no longer stops saving checkpoints for the rest of the session</span></li><li><span>Fixed automatic compaction losing Monitor messages after a model response ended early</span></li><li><span>A prompt that looks like a session-message envelope no longer stops later sessions from saving resume checkpoints</span></li><li><span>A forked chat where the start of one of its own turns could not be written to disk (for example on a full disk) saves checkpoints again after a restart; that turn is left out, and Muse says so once</span></li><li><span>After a subagent message or other background record could not be saved to a full disk, compaction checkpoints work again without restarting the chat</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">session/leave</code> with <code class="docs-code-inline">stop: true</code> no longer releases a session while one of its workflows cannot be stopped (its stop record is in conflict); the leave fails and the session stays with its host, including when you retry it with a new command id; until the host process restarts, such a leave keeps failing (a known limitation)</span></li><li><span>The todo list now stays on screen while a background workflow is still running, instead of disappearing as soon as the turn that launched it ends</span></li><li><span>Notes waiting on a busy subagent now show Queued rows while they wait</span></li><li><span>After a brief storage error in the middle of a task, the chat goes back to saving its progress at the next checkpoint once the error clears, instead of waiting for the task&#x27;s next tool call or its end</span></li><li><span>After a brief disk error interrupts one background save, the chat goes back to saving its progress once the error clears, also when the save had fully reached the disk or belonged to a side chat</span></li><li><span>Loading a forked chat in the app or another client, where the start of one of its own turns could not be written to disk, no longer blocks its checkpoints; that turn is left out, and Muse says so once</span></li><li><span>A chat forked from a compacted chat, where the start of one of its own turns could not be written to disk, can be reopened and continued; that turn is left out, and Muse says so once</span></li><li><span>A compaction that runs while a background task&#x27;s save is still unconfirmed now saves its checkpoint (keeping the older history until the task&#x27;s save resolves) instead of skipping it</span></li><li><span>The <code class="docs-code-inline">game-3d-visuals</code> skill now names each of its pipeline runs, so its first launch is no longer refused and retried</span></li><li><span>Usage limit stops explain when you can continue, and denied requests retain useful error details</span></li><li><span>Pausing a Workflow that has just finished now reports that it already finished and shows its result, instead of leaving the Workflow paused with no result</span></li><li><span>The peer message timeline no longer shows as unavailable after a session accepts a message automatically</span></li></ul><h3 id="performance" class="docs-h docs-h3">Performance<a class="docs-anchor" href="#performance" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Context that hooks add after a prompt or tool call now stays in the conversation where it arrived, so a new hook rule no longer makes the whole conversation re-process on the next model call</span></li><li><span>Reduce repeated session-log bookkeeping while disk writes are failing</span></li><li><span>Starting the app or <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> while other sessions are running uses much less memory, because listing sessions no longer keeps a full copy of each running session&#x27;s history</span></li></ul><h2 id="v1-4-12" class="docs-h docs-h2">1.4.12<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v1-4-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><h3 id="new-1" class="docs-h docs-h3">New<a class="docs-anchor" href="#new-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Added a built-in <code class="docs-code-inline">browser-game</code> skill for building playable browser games from a brief: it sizes the work to the request, plays the game with real input before handoff, and for a long design document runs up to three rounds in which a fresh critic plays a copy of the game against a checklist and the brief&#x27;s rules, fixing what each round finds</span></li><li><span>Permission profiles can open chosen local development ports to sandboxed commands with <code class="docs-code-inline">network.local_ports</code> (<code class="docs-code-inline">allow</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">ask</code>, or <code class="docs-code-inline">deny</code> per port); <code class="docs-code-inline">ask</code> prompts for each connection on Linux and once per session on macOS; a loopback entry in <code class="docs-code-inline">network.targets</code> is now rejected, so move it to <code class="docs-code-inline">network.local_ports</code>; an older Muse build cannot open a chat that saved local-port rules or a managed local-port limit, so update the app to open it (other chats are unaffected)</span></li><li><span>Choose a run preset when starting a session host with <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve --preset</code></span></li></ul><h3 id="improvements-1" class="docs-h docs-h3">Improvements<a class="docs-anchor" href="#improvements-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>After you allow a network request once, the same non-interactive command&#x27;s later requests to that exact host, port, and protocol no longer ask you again while it runs</span></li><li><span>Chats containing saved continuations of finished subagents require a compatible app update; older versions cannot read them</span></li><li><span>Better guidance for carrying research findings and notes into final reports</span></li><li><span>An older Muse build cannot open a chat whose permissions were reset because part of its saved permission history was lost or damaged; update the app to open it (other chats are unaffected)</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/game-3d-visuals</code> finishes in about half the time: it skips the separate visual-plan review and runs one render-vs-reference fix round by default</span></li><li><span>Tiny text, style, or config changes, throwaway prototypes, one-file scripts or pages, and requests for a quick result no longer start by writing a failing test; other fixes run the broad test suite once after the last edit and post a status line during long test runs</span></li></ul><h3 id="fixes-1" class="docs-h docs-h3">Fixes<a class="docs-anchor" href="#fixes-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Deny rules now cover paths that do not exist yet in sandboxed shell commands, blocking their creation without leaving anything behind</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Shell and file tools refuse a workspace root that no longer resolves to its recorded location instead of following it to a new target</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> The Sapling commands the harness runs for you (workspace snapshots, session worktrees) now run inside the sandbox instead of directly on your machine, and session worktrees refuse to run Sapling in a workspace you have not trusted</span></li><li><span>Shell commands can write under every workspace root a session protocol client grants with <code class="docs-code-inline">workspaceRoots</code>, not only the primary root</span></li><li><span>Startup warns again when the configured Bubblewrap path is unusable instead of hiding the sandbox-unavailable notice</span></li><li><span>When a Workflow pause or stop keeps an agent call from starting, its Recovery line and its failed row now say so instead of calling it an internal error and asking for a <code class="docs-code-inline">/feedback</code> report</span></li><li><span>A chat whose tool call could not be written to disk (for example on a full disk) while its result was written can now be forked or given a side chat after a later checkpoint, instead of the fork failing</span></li><li><span>A Workflow agent call whose Agent Definition asks for a model this session doesn&#x27;t offer now runs on the session&#x27;s model instead of failing, and the main agent tells you which calls ran on which model</span></li><li><span>After a <code class="docs-code-inline">session/leave</code> times out, reading that session on the same host works again once its runtime has stopped; until then the read reports that the session is still stopping</span></li><li><span>A <code class="docs-code-inline">session/leave</code> whose accepted reply cannot reach the client now fails at its deadline, instead of holding the session until the connection closes</span></li><li><span>The TUI refreshes the model catalog once in the background when the chosen model is missing from the cache, instead of starting a second refresh</span></li><li><span>Pending approvals and questions in <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve --no-session-log</code> sessions stay readable after the agent starts a subagent</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">session/leave</code> with <code class="docs-code-inline">stop: true</code> now stops a running workflow before it hands the session over, so resuming the session no longer offers to recover the workflow you stopped</span></li><li><span>Subagent crash recovery reports missing tool results as unknown without automatically rerunning the calls</span></li><li><span>Over <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code>, resending a finished turn&#x27;s <code class="docs-code-inline">turn/start</code> with the same command id after a restart returns its original reply instead of a command id conflict</span></li><li><span>When a finished reply or a subagent result cannot be saved, Muse retries briefly, then shows a clear error that says why new messages are refused instead of retrying silently every second</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/permissions</code> now names why a permission change could not be saved</span></li><li><span>When a sandboxed shell command fails writing outside the session&#x27;s writable roots (for example a cache under the home directory failing with <code class="docs-code-inline">Read-only file system</code>), the failure now explains that the sandbox blocked it and names the <code class="docs-code-inline">workspace_roots</code> grant, a one-time unsandboxed run, and workspace-or-<code class="docs-code-inline">/tmp</code> cache options, instead of the raw filesystem error</span></li><li><span>In the terminal app, a chat where the start of one turn could not be written to disk (for example on a full disk) no longer loses every later checkpoint after a restart; that turn is set aside, and Muse says so once</span></li><li><span>Sessions wake once the blocking run settles after a background task finishes while the session is busy</span></li><li><span>Rewinding to before a turn that failed, or whose end could not be saved (for example on a full disk), now works instead of every attempt being refused, and a turn that can never be rewound is shown as unavailable instead of offered</span></li><li><span>Opening a subagent&#x27;s detail view now loads the child&#x27;s transcript from the child&#x27;s own session and keeps it live while open</span></li><li><span>Keep long requests running with their full context when compaction fails</span></li><li><span>When a Workflow pause or stop keeps an agent call from starting, its Recovery line and its failed row now end with what you can do: &quot;Start the Workflow again if it is still needed.&quot;</span></li><li><span>On EdenFS checkouts, <code class="docs-code-inline">sl</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">hg</code> commands need the launcher (sandbox disabled) to reach Eden state; the native sandbox no longer grants Eden filesystem or socket access</span></li><li><span>Rewinding to a turn after one that was still running when the chat saved a checkpoint now works, instead of every such rewind being refused after you confirm it</span></li><li><span>Goal sessions waiting on external work wait on a change watcher instead of appearing stopped</span></li><li><span>Stopping background work from a notification now works instead of reporting it was not found</span></li><li><span>A chat that lost two saves in one turn on a full disk (a tool result, then the next tool call) can be reopened again; the affected turn is set aside instead of blocking the whole chat</span></li><li><span>A prompt sent while the session view is stale-idle steers into the active background delivery over the session protocol instead of starting a duplicate fresh run</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/game-3d-visuals</code> now starts on its own only for polished 3D work (a reference image, Blender, or an explicit high-fidelity ask); quick 3D pages and games are built directly instead of waiting on its multi-agent pipeline</span></li><li><span>Rewinding to a turn after the conversation was compacted now works, instead of every such rewind being refused</span></li><li><span>Keep interrupted startup from leaving a partially created session</span></li><li><span>A subagent stop that was interrupted right after it took effect no longer leaves that subagent stuck: the next open completes the stop&#x27;s record, and if that record cannot be written the session still opens and the next open retries</span></li><li><span>Startup fails with a clear error when the configured Linux sandbox helper path is unusable instead of silently starting unsandboxed</span></li><li><span>After a crash, a message you sent to replace Muse&#x27;s current reply, or one Muse showed as queued while it was busy, is no longer treated as done: retrying it now says it was abandoned instead of claiming it already ran</span></li><li><span>Apps built on the Muse SDKs now see the new turn a Replace starts as the running turn (the session snapshot&#x27;s <code class="docs-code-inline">activeTurn</code>) instead of no running turn</span></li><li><span>In apps that open chats through the Muse session server, a chat where the start of one turn could not be written to disk (for example on a full disk) no longer loses later checkpoints after it is reopened; that turn is set aside, and Muse says so once</span></li><li><span>Fork and side chat no longer fail with an internal error when the system is under load</span></li><li><span>Forking a session at an earlier turn keeps exactly the turns up to that turn instead of refusing the cut (some compacted sessions and forks of forks still refuse the cut or fork from a later turn, and a cut that keeps no turns of an older session still refuses while that session is open)</span></li><li><span>After a reply or an ordinary tool result could not be saved to a full disk, compaction checkpoints work again without restarting the chat</span></li><li><span>Fixed degraded session recovery losing the latest workspace root set</span></li><li><span>After a mid-reply compaction, the TUI no longer fires a needless second auto-compaction on the stale Blocked pressure reading</span></li><li><span>Hooks set with <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve -c hooks.…</code> now run in served sessions instead of being silently dropped</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">pip install muse-code-sdk</code> now also installs its companion wire-types package, so <code class="docs-code-inline">import muse_code</code> works in a fresh Python environment</span></li><li><span>When one write to a side chat&#x27;s file fails (for example on a full disk), the main chat keeps saving its progress and can still be forked once the problem clears, instead of staying unable to save until restart</span></li><li><span>The first manual compaction in a side chat now works, including after resuming it</span></li><li><span>A user review gate now explicitly defers outward-facing actions until post-inspection approval, so bounded steps stop instead of running ahead into tracker and chat writes</span></li><li><span>Idle sessions reliably wake when a background task finishes</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/plan</code> on a small change now plans instead of implementing it, the skill keys the explicit case on how its body arrived, so implement-shaped task text is read as the planning subject, not an implement request</span></li><li><span>With MCP servers configured, using <code class="docs-code-inline">/side</code> before your first message (for example right after resuming) no longer stops every later message before it reaches the model; a side chat you open with <code class="docs-code-inline">/side</code> now runs without MCP tools</span></li><li><span>A chat whose Workflow result could not be saved (for example on a full disk) and that then ran another tool now reopens in the same app session after a restart, instead of failing to open</span></li><li><span>When a write to a background helper session&#x27;s file fails once (for example on a full disk) right after it starts, its later writes and checkpoints go through once the problem clears, instead of staying refused until restart</span></li><li><span>Older builds keep reading durable session records after a newer build adds a member, instead of failing the whole session read</span></li><li><span>A workflow that ended after its durable fact write failed no longer stays listed as running forever in the bottom work list; its row now shows the failed or cancelled result and clears after the usual grace</span></li><li><span>On macOS, Muse Code no longer freezes when the Keychain stops answering: it stops waiting after 5 seconds and says your login is still saved, and <code class="docs-code-inline">muse --help</code> no longer waits on the Keychain</span></li><li><span>A sandboxed shell command killed mid-run no longer breaks the next command with the same deny rules; its leftover empty placeholder is now cleaned up automatically</span></li><li><span>Notes sent to a running subagent now show a Delivered row once the child picks them up</span></li><li><span>After a full disk, starting a new chat no longer retries the previous chat&#x27;s unsaved run ending in the new chat</span></li><li><span>When a brief storage failure, such as a full disk, keeps the session log from saving a new Workflow agent call&#x27;s start even after its one retry, only that call now fails, with a plain reason, and the rest of the Workflow keeps running; before, the whole Workflow ended</span></li><li><span>A chat where the start of one turn could not be written to disk (for example on a full disk) can be forked and can open a side chat again; the new chat leaves out that one turn, and Muse says so once</span></li><li><span>If a Workflow subagent switches model or has a wake-up refused and you cancel your next turn before it starts, the turn after it still tells you about it</span></li><li><span>On an ephemeral <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> host, replaying the original <code class="docs-code-inline">session/start</code> of a session that <code class="docs-code-inline">session/leave</code> released now answers the original acknowledgement without bringing the removed session back</span></li><li><span>After a full disk cancelled a workflow run, a later background result on that run no longer stops checkpoints until a restart</span></li><li><span>Failed <code class="docs-code-inline">/feedback</code> uploads now show the reason returned by the server instead of only the status code</span></li><li><span>When a chat is stuck retrying a save that failed, <code class="docs-code-inline">/new</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">/clear</code> and other new sessions from it, local-model setup and a provider key swap now fail at once with the &quot;saving failed … retrying automatically&quot; message instead of waiting quietly or saving a rejection, and the same command works once the chat recovers</span></li><li><span>Sessions served by <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> that use a goal keep saving context checkpoints, so they resume quickly again</span></li><li><span>A chat where the start of one turn could not be written to disk (for example on a full disk) can be rewound again; the rewind leaves out that one turn, and Muse says so once</span></li><li><span>Workflow guidance keeps large-result details ahead of lengthy research notes</span></li><li><span>When a background save to the chat file is cut short by a brief I/O error and never retried, the chat goes back to saving its progress once the problem clears, instead of staying unable to save until restart</span></li><li><span>Resume and history show the finished marker for background terminal completions served over the session protocol, matching the live view</span></li><li><span>A <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> chat whose saved view on disk is damaged or unreadable (for example a torn <code class="docs-code-inline">HEAD.json</code>, a missing journal file, or history a newer build wrote) is rebuilt from its session log while it is being resumed, so that resume shows the whole history instead of no history, and the chat never needs reopening</span></li><li><span>Reminder checks no longer repeat after their decision when a Stop or PreToolUse hook blocks them</span></li><li><span>Side chats retain the original conversation after a checkpoint</span></li><li><span>A forked chat where the start of one of its own turns could not be written to disk (for example on a full disk) can be reopened and continued again; that turn is left out, and Muse says so once</span></li><li><span>When one save to the chat file fails because the file could not be opened or read (a brief I/O error), the chat goes back to saving its progress as soon as the problem clears, instead of staying unable to save until restart</span></li><li><span>Forking a session over the session protocol no longer intermittently reports the new session is already in use</span></li><li><span>Quitting the TUI no longer prints internal cleanup or shutdown diagnostics to the terminal; they now go to the local diagnostic log</span></li><li><span>Worktree creation and cleanup stay sandboxed in unprivileged containers, using an empty read-only process view where the container refuses a fresh one</span></li><li><span>After a one-time storage error leaves a background task&#x27;s save unconfirmed, the session&#x27;s periodic context checkpoints keep landing instead of being refused until restart</span></li><li><span>A tool result or other chat record whose save failed while the disk was full is saved again at the session&#x27;s next step if there is room by then, so a restart after that keeps it</span></li><li><span>A chat that was never compacted and whose saved log has an unreadable or missing line in the middle now opens for reading in apps that use the session protocol, showing everything that can be read with a notice at the spot, instead of refusing the whole chat; continuing or forking such a chat is still refused for now</span></li><li><span>When another agent&#x27;s start could not be confirmed as saved just as a Workflow starts a new agent call, that call now fails on its own with a plain reason; while session storage is still failing, the Workflow still stops at its next save</span></li><li><span>When saving a checkpoint is interrupted twice in a row by a brief I/O error, the chat (and a reminder helper) now cleans up the half-written save and keeps saving its progress once the problem clears, instead of staying unable to save until it is reopened</span></li><li><span>Resumed sessions exit after the run finishes instead of hanging when an earlier denied tool approval predates the session&#x27;s latest checkpoint</span></li><li><span>When the same configuration, environment or step-limit error stops two turns back to back with nothing shown between them, it now appears once while the session runs, as it already does after a resume</span></li></ul><h3 id="performance-1" class="docs-h docs-h3">Performance<a class="docs-anchor" href="#performance-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>In <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code>, leaving a session and shutting the host down no longer reread the whole chat history to report its final position</span></li><li><span>Long sessions store repeated setup blocks once, so logs stay small and resume loads faster</span></li></ul><h2 id="v1-4-11" class="docs-h docs-h2">1.4.11<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v1-4-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><h3 id="new-2" class="docs-h docs-h3">Improvements<a class="docs-anchor" href="#improvements-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Workflow agents receive source and field crash</span></li><li><span>Service and loop restarts verify every process against an ownership record before stopping it, so look-alike sessions are left running</span></li><li><span>After Muse restarts from a crash, a subagent the agent started directly (not from a workflow) that had not started running yet is no longer started again by itself; its parent gets one result saying the outcome gains <code class="docs-code-inline">view/gap</code>, so code that matches it exhaustively needs a new case</span></li><li><span>Report tasks that finish during <code class="docs-code-inline">/stop all</code> as already finished instead of failing the stop</span></li><li><span>Workflow agents now get a notice when the summary list omits earlier results, even when full results are class="docs-anchor" href="#v1-4-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><h3 id="new-3" class="docs-h docs-h3">New<a class="docs-anchor" href="#new-3" aria-hidden="true" class="docs-code-inline">XDG_CONFIG_HOME</code></span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> The git skill now refuses to hide your untracked files with ignore rules or a stash when a task only asks for a clean tree</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Hook input <code class="docs-code-inline">model_provider</code> now names the vendor of the selected model instead of the connection it was routed through: it is <code class="docs-code-inline">meta</code> only for a model the built-in Meta gateway catalog lists as Meta-owned, and is omitted otherwise, so a Claude or GPT session on the Meta gateway no longer reports <code class="docs-code-inline">meta</code></span></li><li><span>A duplicate wait for a background command that is still running no longer holds the chat for its full requested wait</span></li><li><span>A Workflow child that stops because its start record can&#x27;t be saved, or because a different start record was already saved for it, now says in plain words that nothing new ran, that the other Workflow children keep running, and what to do next</span></li><li><span>A Workflow task that was interrupted right after it scheduled a retry now resumes with its recorded model and effort instead of being held</span></li><li><span>Resuming a session whose log cannot prove its last start is refused with a message naming the broken record instead of opening silently</span></li><li><span>SessionStart hooks run on every resumed TUI session whose log proves its last start, reporting <code class="docs-code-inline">resume</code> (or <code class="docs-code-inline">fork</code> for a never-activated clone) as their source; a replayed copy that cannot prove it runs none and says so in its startup notice</span></li><li><span>Spawn rejection hints now explain the reason in plain words instead of internal enum names</span></li><li><span>Repository-wide Sapling file listings (<code class="docs-code-inline">hg files</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">hg locate</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">hg manifest</code>) on EdenFS checkouts are refused before they hang, pointing at <code class="docs-code-inline">search</code> or <code class="docs-code-inline">hg biggrep</code> instead</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> now shows the history of a session that Muse 1.4.8 is still running, instead of failing to read it until that session closes</span></li><li><span>Sessions started through the session protocol honor saved reasoning effort</span></li><li><span>Workflow messages and exit prompts keep the recorded name after resume</span></li><li><span>A monitor you start now appears in the footer and in <code class="docs-code-inline">/tasks</code> right away, even when the machine is busy or the disk is slow</span></li><li><span>A forked chat whose history has a background-task notice delivered mid-turn now opens in apps and SDKs in more cases, instead of failing to load</span></li><li><span>When a <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> client resumes a chat whose saved history view file was deleted, the chat shows its history again instead of none</span></li><li><span>Manual <code class="docs-code-inline">/compact</code> now compacts sessions with MCP servers configured, instead of answering &quot;no compactable run is available&quot;</span></li><li><span>An MCP server whose process stays alive but never responds during startup now fails with <code class="docs-code-inline">the server did not respond during startup</code> instead of the generic operation timeout</span></li><li><span>Switching a conversation between the desktop app and the terminal when they run different versions of Muse Code now catches up a short exchange made on the other side instead of rebuilding its saved history from scratch; the first open after updating from a release before 1.4.9 still rebuilds it once</span></li><li><span>When a resumed Workflow task&#x27;s first save fails before anything is written, only that task retries instead of the whole Workflow stopping; if the retry&#x27;s save fails too, only that task fails and tells you what to do next</span></li><li><span>A context compaction no longer skips its checkpoint when another session write lands while that checkpoint is being saved</span></li><li><span>Running /compact in a chat whose turns all ended before any model request (for example, a message cancelled before Muse began preparing its model request) now reports that there is nothing to summarize instead of writing a summary checkpoint that could later let the chat skip setting up its developer instructions</span></li><li><span>Resuming a thread whose saved history had fallen far behind now brings it up to date in that same resume, instead of showing no history and missing live replies until the next resume</span></li><li><span>A session whose model reused a tool call id for two same-length results no longer becomes impossible to resume or compact after old tool results are cleared</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> keeps answering other requests while a long session&#x27;s history loads for the first time, and resuming a session that is still loading waits for it instead of reporting the session as in use</span></li><li><span>Subagents now honor the reasoning effort set in their agent definition</span></li><li><span>A turn whose final answer consists only of the &quot;[Previous turn ended without an assistant reply.]&quot; marker now gets one bounded re-prompt for a real reply, and the marker is stripped from run summaries</span></li><li><span>Compaction keeps working after you reopen a saved chat, instead of summarizing again at every boundary and eventually failing with &quot;could not prepare the conversation&quot;</span></li><li><span>The TypeScript and Python SDKs no longer mark a turn retracted, or drop its completion, when its retract is declined; in the TypeScript SDK, <code class="docs-code-inline">StaleDroppableMethod</code> gains <code class="docs-code-inline">turn/retracted</code>, so code that matches it exhaustively needs a new case</span></li><li><span>Workflow control rooms and opened results keep the recorded workflow name</span></li><li><span>Retrying a fork with the same command id now returns the original outcome instead of answering command_id_conflict, matching gate-off idempotency; reusing a command id with a different cut still conflicts</span></li><li><span>Newly saved workflow history and live updates use recorded names, with &quot;name unavailable&quot; for older runs that have none</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> keeps answering other requests while it resumes or forks a long session, opens a side chat on one, lists its pending approvals or reads one of its tool outputs, instead of stalling every other thread until that session&#x27;s history is read</span></li><li><span>A Workflow subagent that named your session&#x27;s model keeps running after a restart even when that model is now hidden or missing from the model list, the same as one that left the model out</span></li><li><span>Subagents use their definition&#x27;s model, falling back to the session model with a notice when unavailable</span></li><li><span>A long goal run no longer stops early when fresh next-step guidance replaces still-active guidance after new tool work; identical guidance still stops as before</span></li><li><span>When <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> starts with no saved model list and your account still needs a payment method, onboarding or age confirmation, turns now say what to do instead of asking you to log in again</span></li><li><span>The transcript no longer shows a &quot;◆ [Previous turn ended without an assistant reply.]&quot; row, a reply containing only that resume marker renders nothing, and a real answer prefixed by it shows just the answer</span></li><li><span>The bundled Three.js skill now gives a working WebGPU post-processing example instead of one that imports a file current three.js no longer ships</span></li><li><span>Allow subagents to process pending results while the parent waits</span></li><li><span>A Workflow resumed after a crash no longer shows a killed agent as still running when its relaunch is refused before it starts; the killed attempt&#x27;s row now ends Failed and the Workflow completes</span></li><li><span>Correct <code class="docs-code-inline">/compact</code> token counts when tool results are cleared or reminders expire</span></li></ul><h3 id="performance-3" class="docs-h docs-h3">Performance<a class="docs-anchor" href="#performance-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/btw</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">/side</code>, and <code class="docs-code-inline">/fork</code> open faster in very large compacted sessions</span></li><li><span>Reduce memory use when loading sessions with repeated approval records</span></li></ul><h2 id="v1-4-9" class="docs-h docs-h2">1.4.9<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v1-4-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><h3 id="new-4" class="docs-h docs-h3">New<a class="docs-anchor" href="#new-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">--disable-request-user-input</code> (TUI, <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code>) withholds <code class="docs-code-inline">request_user_input</code> from the main conversation (side chats keep it), so an unattended run never stops to wait on a question; a call naming it gets an unavailable-tool error instead. <code class="docs-code-inline">--yolo</code> implies the flag on the TUI and <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code></span></li><li><span>Every MCP <code class="docs-code-inline">tools/call</code> Muse sends carries the model&#x27;s tool-call id in <code class="docs-code-inline">_meta.callId</code> (and the idempotency key when set), so an MCP server can correlate it with the session&#x27;s tool-call item and dedupe retries</span></li><li><span>Session-protocol clients receive an <code class="docs-code-inline">approval/reviewing</code> view event while the built-in Auto-review reviewer holds an approval, so a UI can show that the request is under review without asking the user to decide it</span></li><li><span>Tool-call items in <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> sessions carry the words a tool declares for the call, with running, done and neutral forms, so apps can say what a call does instead of showing the tool name</span></li></ul><h3 id="improvements-4" class="docs-h docs-h3">Improvements<a class="docs-anchor" href="#improvements-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Session-protocol clients: view cursors are now minted in the <code class="docs-code-inline">v4:</code> spelling; a cursor in the previous <code class="docs-code-inline">v3:</code> spelling is refused once with the standard &quot;reopen without a cursor&quot; guidance, and a view cache saved under the previous generation is rebuilt on first use, so no client silently skips events now that the Auto-review hold folds its own <code class="docs-code-inline">approval/reviewing</code> event into older sessions</span></li></ul><h3 id="fixes-4" class="docs-h docs-h3">Fixes<a class="docs-anchor" href="#fixes-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Sapling commands now work inside the sandboxed shell on EdenFS checkouts</span></li><li><span>Clear interrupt status when the interrupted run ends</span></li><li><span>Long sessions no longer summarize the same history again at every turn when a context checkpoint cannot be saved</span></li><li><span>Long sessions with an active goal that start more than one subagent compact their context again, instead of retrying a summary on every turn that never takes effect</span></li><li><span>Contributor-mode requests with no served model list yet now consistently carry the contributor signal</span></li><li><span>When <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> starts without a saved model list and the provider rejects your saved key or sign-in, turns now fail with a sign-in-required error that apps can act on, and reloading the session works once the key is fixed, with no restart</span></li><li><span>On a <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> host running the native Auto-review reviewer, an approval the reviewer was holding is handed to the human client when the turn ends before the reviewer decides, and one recovered after a host restart is presented instead of staying hidden; a request the reviewer hands over says so (<code class="docs-code-inline">judgeEscalated</code>)</span></li><li><span>Rechecks conversation history and restored context before applying a background summary</span></li><li><span>When a skill you named cannot load, the agent now stops and asks instead of improvising</span></li><li><span>Hooks and MCP servers now receive <code class="docs-code-inline">PROVENANCE_PROVIDER_SCOPE</code> when the app that launched the session set it</span></li><li><span>Allow one more attempt to clear old tool results after reopening a session whose required compaction failed</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> now closes the open approval of a subagent that has no session log of its own (for example one started by an earlier version) when a session that has not been compacted is resumed after a crash, so a late decision on it reports that it is already resolved instead of not found</span></li><li><span>A <code class="docs-code-inline">/goal</code> replace question now appears even while a run waits for admission, instead of the submit being silently dropped</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> answers <code class="docs-code-inline">plugin/install</code> and the <code class="docs-code-inline">plugin/marketplace*</code> methods for an existing session it has not loaded with <code class="docs-code-inline">sessionNotLoaded</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">sessionInUse</code> or <code class="docs-code-inline">sessionAmbiguous</code> instead of <code class="docs-code-inline">sessionNotFound</code>, so a client no longer treats a stored session as gone</span></li><li><span>After a compaction whose history clean-up was refused, the next model step no longer fails with &quot;Origin read requires valid checkpoint-suffix ...&quot;</span></li></ul><h3 id="performance-4" class="docs-h docs-h3">Performance<a class="docs-anchor" href="#performance-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>While idle, <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> no longer rewrites the lock file of every old empty session it has to keep, or re-reads most sessions it cannot list, every few seconds</span></li><li><span>Typing stays responsive in long sessions with many subagents</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> answers a <code class="docs-code-inline">session/resume</code> that carries a known cursor by reading only the events after that cursor, instead of the whole session history. This includes a cursor taken from a streaming delta, which now resumes after the event it streams from. Such a resume of a session whose history exceeds the 64 MiB read limit now gets its new events instead of <code class="docs-code-inline">noneReason: projectionReadLimit</code></span></li></ul><h2 id="v1-4-8" class="docs-h docs-h2">1.4.8<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v1-4-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><h3 id="new-5" class="docs-h docs-h3">New<a class="docs-anchor" href="#new-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Pick the permission profile when resuming a served session with the <code class="docs-code-inline">permissionProfile</code> member of <code class="docs-code-inline">session/resume</code> (and the SDK resume option); an id the host does not offer is refused before anything is written</span></li><li><span>Muse now saves a note when cleanup after a finished turn keeps failing; an older Muse build cannot open a chat that contains this note, so update the app to open it (other chats are unaffected)</span></li><li><span>The Linux sandbox helper plants in-namespace loopback listeners for listed local ports and bridges them to host loopback (delivery half of <code class="docs-code-inline">network.local_ports</code>; the profile verdict map itself lands with the agent side)</span></li><li><span>Session protocol now serves the model&#x27;s narration between tool calls as <code class="docs-code-inline">agentMessage</code> items, and every completed <code class="docs-code-inline">agentMessage</code> says whether it is commentary or the final answer (<code class="docs-code-inline">messagePhase</code>); the Python wire-types package has the matching typed field; view cursors saved by an earlier version are refused (<code class="docs-code-inline">-32011</code> with reason <code class="docs-code-inline">missingAnchor</code>; the resume guide covers the reopen)</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">--preset empty</code> starts a session with no built-in tools; the model gets only the tools of MCP servers you configured</span></li><li><span>Apps connected to <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> can follow a running subagent live by subscribing to its session, and unsubscribing from a subagent session no longer fails</span></li><li><span>Monitor feed lines are recorded as <code class="docs-code-inline">monitorFeed</code> items; builds older than this change cannot open a chat containing one (updating fixes it)</span></li></ul><h3 id="improvements-5" class="docs-h docs-h3">Improvements<a class="docs-anchor" href="#improvements-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">skill/list</code> rows include an optional <code class="docs-code-inline">title</code> with the name a skill declares for people to read, beside the unchanged <code class="docs-code-inline">displayName</code></span></li><li><span>When a plugin hook finishes, helper processes it left running in the background are stopped so the plugin&#x27;s installed files can be released; hooks configured in settings keep their existing background-helper behavior</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">SessionStart</code> hooks report <code class="docs-code-inline">clear</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">compact</code> as their source on the runtime&#x27;s own <code class="docs-code-inline">/clear</code> and compaction boundaries, so a hook that matches only <code class="docs-code-inline">startup</code> no longer runs there</span></li><li><span>A permission-profile change made over the session protocol records the client&#x27;s name on the durable audit fact and in the experimental <code class="docs-code-inline">session/permissionProfileChanged</code> notification; a forked session&#x27;s own fork entry carries no name until the child records a change of its own, and the fork is refused when the parent&#x27;s retained history and live state disagree on the recorded name; an older Muse build cannot open a chat whose permission profile a newer build changed, so update the app to open it (other chats are unaffected)</span></li><li><span>Auto-review now hands an action to you for approval once the reviewer has used 15 steps without reaching a decision, instead of letting a single review run for dozens of steps and use many tokens</span></li></ul><h3 id="fixes-5" class="docs-h docs-h3">Fixes<a class="docs-anchor" href="#fixes-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> sessions started after the startup model list finishes loading, or after a login, use the sandbox the server checked at startup instead of checking it again for every session</span></li><li><span>Repeated status lines between commands no longer flood the transcript; the commands fold into one row</span></li><li><span>Resuming a session after its latest run was interrupted keeps the earlier title and history readable</span></li><li><span>Resuming a session keeps earlier run history readable after a later run replaces it</span></li><li><span>Paging through a large tool output in a <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> client no longer re-reads the whole session for every later page while the session log is unchanged</span></li><li><span>Resuming a session again in the same <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> process after its earlier load ended without a clean shutdown now reports the session as in use instead of risking a damaged session log</span></li><li><span>Forking a session with no turns yet no longer fails when background cleanup runs at the same moment</span></li><li><span>A question asked during goal-carried work without its own timeout now times out after 5 minutes (recorded as timed_out; no answer is chosen for you) instead of parking the run indefinitely; touching the prompt still cancels that safety deadline, and ordinary interactive questions keep waiting with no deadline</span></li><li><span>Claude plugins whose command files are up to 256 KiB now install</span></li><li><span>The verify reminder no longer pushes the agent past a question it asked you; it nudges only when the agent calls work done without running it</span></li><li><span>Sessions keep the selected model&#x27;s output limit after model changes and reloads</span></li><li><span>Resuming a session keeps compaction usable after a later run takes over</span></li><li><span>Over <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code>, a session that lost saved records now opens with the rest of its history instead of failing with &quot;projection unavailable&quot;</span></li><li><span>The startup trust prompt no longer times out under terminals that report the cursor slowly, such as Zellij</span></li><li><span>Preserve measured context usage when resuming a session</span></li><li><span>After Muse restarts, a Workflow agent call whose saved start record is missing or incomplete, or whose agent definition is gone or no longer matches how the call started, now fails on its own with a result that says what happened and what to do next, instead of failing the whole Workflow</span></li><li><span>Running plugin hooks and MCP servers keep their original installed files available through completion and child cleanup when a newer plugin version is installed</span></li><li><span>Workflow subagents that pick their own model keep working when you resume a session with <code class="docs-code-inline">--model</code> and later resume it without the flag (sessions resumed with <code class="docs-code-inline">--model</code> on an earlier version are not repaired)</span></li><li><span>Startup notices for MCP servers the managed policy does not admit now appear even when a required MCP server fails to start</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">sl</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">hg</code> commands that use globs or braces, such as <code class="docs-code-inline">sl status *.rs</code>, now ask for approval like <code class="docs-code-inline">git</code> commands do</span></li><li><span>Read-only Sapling commands such as <code class="docs-code-inline">sl status</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">sl log</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">hg diff</code> are now treated like their <code class="docs-code-inline">git</code> equivalents</span></li><li><span>Resuming a workflow after tbh stopped no longer fails the whole run when an agent call was still waiting for a free agent slot; that call now starts normally</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse resume</code> no longer refuses a session whose journal head was pruned when a checkpoint anchors the suffix; the no-anchor case names the recovery</span></li><li><span>Sessions that <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> recorded under the old <code class="docs-code-inline">muse</code> provider label keep their reasoning after a model change and a restart, instead of dropping it or failing every turn once compacted</span></li><li><span>Resuming a workflow no longer requires repeating its name</span></li><li><span>Runtime-owned child runs (branches, side chats, subagents) no longer re-fire the root session&#x27;s <code class="docs-code-inline">SessionStart</code> hooks</span></li><li><span>Prompt hints and away recaps wait for a session&#x27;s SessionStart hooks to finish before they run</span></li><li><span>Fix completed workflows reappearing as running after resuming a compacted session</span></li><li><span>Plan files under .agents/plans/ no longer raise an approval card, the directory is an ordinary writable workspace path, while the rest of .agents stays protected</span></li><li><span>When Muse resumes a Workflow after a restart and the script finishes without waiting for an agent call that Muse held back, Muse now tells you which call did not run, why, and what to do next, instead of reporting plain success</span></li><li><span>When a chat is stuck retrying a save that failed, <code class="docs-code-inline">!</code> shell commands, <code class="docs-code-inline">/compact</code> and new turns over <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> now fail at once with the &quot;saving failed … retrying automatically&quot; message instead of a busy answer</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> now re-asks a pending approval with <code class="docs-code-inline">approval/request</code> when a multi-stage approval moves on to its next stage, and when a client replays its <code class="docs-code-inline">session/start</code> after a host restart, so session protocol clients see the prompt instead of a turn that waits forever</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code> waits for context compaction to finish before exiting, so resumed sessions keep their compacted summary</span></li><li><span>On Windows, renaming a session now fails with a plain &quot;not supported on this platform&quot; error (<code class="docs-code-inline">session/rename is not supported on this platform</code>) instead of an internal one, and a client that requests the new <code class="docs-code-inline">sessionRename</code> capability at connect time learns that rename is unavailable there. <code class="docs-code-inline">CapabilityName</code> gains a <code class="docs-code-inline">SessionRename</code> variant; exhaustive matches on it need a new arm</span></li><li><span>A session whose MCP startup could not be audited (its open record was missing or unreadable) now shows one startup notice for each MCP server the managed policy did not admit, beside the audit-failed notice; a session whose every server was refused, which showed nothing before, now shows those notices too</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/goal</code> changes no longer freeze the TUI on long sessions; repeat Goal edits now re-read only newly committed run records instead of rescanning every run stream</span></li><li><span>Compacting a session keeps the request detail the summary needs, so manual compaction rebuilds the exact prefix instead of falling back to a bounded summary</span></li><li><span>Startup selection now skips a PATH-discovered system Bubblewrap copy that does not advertise every required capability and uses the embedded copy instead; an explicit override missing one fails closed naming the flag</span></li><li><span>Resending a request after a restart returns the original result instead of running it twice</span></li><li><span>With contributor mode ON, requests route to the family&#x27;s <code class="docs-code-inline">-contributor</code> model as soon as a fresh served catalog shows it, including mid-session logins, background refreshes, and late-appearing siblings, instead of sticking to the base model on a stale list</span></li><li><span>A session whose saved images or videos have wider folder or file permissions than the app creates now resumes, and its videos still send</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">tbh serve -c</code> settings such as <code class="docs-code-inline">endpoint_transport.base_url</code> now reach the model provider instead of being silently ignored</span></li><li><span>Opening the transcript link of a memory-only reminder helper, while its chat is open and the helper ran since the chat was opened, now says the helper kept no transcript and names its chat, instead of &quot;session not found&quot;</span></li><li><span>Explain context compaction failures in plain language</span></li><li><span>Over <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code>, retrying <code class="docs-code-inline">turn/start</code> with the same command id but a different message or options while that turn is still parked (replacing a running turn, waiting for the running turn to finish, or waiting behind a reminder) now fails with <code class="docs-code-inline">command_id_conflict</code> instead of being treated as the original turn</span></li><li><span>Sessions named more than once (an automatic name counts) open with their full history every time instead of sometimes showing an empty transcript</span></li><li><span>Keep <code class="docs-code-inline">/side</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">/btw</code> progress visible while a side chat is starting</span></li><li><span>SessionStart hook runs no longer appear as <code class="docs-code-inline">hookRun</code> items in the session view stream</span></li><li><span>Concurrent resumes of a <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> session no longer run its SessionStart hooks twice</span></li><li><span>Turning off Contributor mode in settings now fully opts out, including background requests</span></li><li><span>Keep pending results from an earlier turn intact when the next model response is cut off</span></li><li><span>A compacted chat whose saved history file was damaged or deleted shows its full history again after the next resume instead of staying empty; a forked chat in that state now says why it cannot resume instead of opening with no history</span></li><li><span>The permission-profile refusal announced early in the 1.4.6 notes takes effect in this release: profiles the live session cannot enforce are now refused when chosen at launch (<code class="docs-code-inline">--permission-profile</code> or the configured default) instead of silently collapsing to read-only; the refusal names each offending rule with the reason and a remedy (remove or adjust it, or set the temporary escape hatch to run with it unenforced and a warning). Profiles that keep a built-in profile&#x27;s filesystem rules, <code class="docs-code-inline">:unrestricted</code> included, keep working; profiles that add or change filesystem rules (deny rules included), add <code class="docs-code-inline">workspace_roots</code>, or add Unix-socket rules are refused, most users can delete those rules and relaunch</span></li></ul><h3 id="performance-5" class="docs-h docs-h3">Performance<a class="docs-anchor" href="#performance-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Long sessions no longer spend more time on every frame keeping the session token totals up to date</span></li><li><span>Large batches of parallel tool calls now land their results without rescanning the transcript for each one</span></li><li><span>Bash command results no longer repeat the command back to the model, so a long inline script takes up context once instead of twice</span></li><li><span>Task panel refreshes stay fast in long sessions with many finished tasks</span></li><li><span>Opening a long older session for the first time now rebuilds its history many times faster</span></li></ul><h2 id="v1-4-7" class="docs-h docs-h2">1.4.7<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v1-4-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><h3 id="new-6" class="docs-h docs-h3">New<a class="docs-anchor" href="#new-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> now tells session protocol apps on <code class="docs-code-inline">initialize</code> whether this machine can enforce the shell sandbox and, when it cannot, why; the Python wire-types package has the matching typed fields</span></li><li><span>A skill can set <code class="docs-code-inline">metadata.display-name</code> in its <code class="docs-code-inline">SKILL.md</code>; the transcript&#x27;s skill rows and the <code class="docs-code-inline">/skills</code> list then show that name instead of the skill&#x27;s id</span></li><li><span>Terminals that support program status reports (OSC 7501) can now show whether a session is working, waiting for you, or done</span></li><li><span>The agent can now generate and edit images when your model catalog includes an image model</span></li></ul><h3 id="improvements-6" class="docs-h docs-h3">Improvements<a class="docs-anchor" href="#improvements-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/goal cancel</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">/goal stop</code> now clear the goal like <code class="docs-code-inline">/goal clear</code>, and <code class="docs-code-inline">/goal</code> subcommands ignore case</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/goal &lt;objective&gt;</code> now asks before replacing an unfinished goal; Esc keeps the current goal and your typed text</span></li><li><span>Menus consistently use <code class="docs-code-inline">⟩</code> to mark the focused choice</span></li></ul><h3 id="fixes-6" class="docs-h docs-h3">Fixes<a class="docs-anchor" href="#fixes-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Resuming a session saved by an older version no longer sets aside one earlier turn&#x27;s history on the next resume, including sessions an affected version already resumed</span></li><li><span>Manual /compact on a short conversation now summarizes the full history instead of installing an empty summary beside it</span></li><li><span>Stopping a subagent the agent is waiting on no longer makes the agent report the stopped result again in an extra turn</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">session/list</code> now includes a session that another Muse Code process, such as an open TUI, is using; its details catch up as that session settles, and resuming it is still refused as in use</span></li><li><span>Long-running <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> sessions no longer use a little more memory with every turn</span></li><li><span>A context compaction now always saves its resume checkpoint together with it; if the checkpoint cannot be written, the compaction is skipped and retried at the next step instead of leaving a session that resumes slowly</span></li><li><span>Clarify known turn errors while preserving sign-in guidance</span></li><li><span>Preserve pending tool results when a model rejects a large request</span></li><li><span>When a turn dies and its failure cannot be saved, a message sent after the quick retries run out (about 30 seconds) now returns a clear &quot;saving failed: &lt;cause&gt;; retrying automatically&quot; error instead of being silently held, and the chat unlocks by itself as soon as a retry (once a minute) saves the failure</span></li><li><span>When a tool panics with a text message while the turn waits on it, its failed result now includes that message (<code class="docs-code-inline">tool task panicked: &lt;message&gt;</code>) instead of only <code class="docs-code-inline">tool task panicked</code></span></li><li><span>Forked conversations can continue after their first compaction</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> refuses a session whose permission profile needs the automated reviewer up front, with the reviewer-unavailable reason, when it starts without a saved model list and then falls back to logged-out mode, as it does on a logged-out start</span></li><li><span>After <code class="docs-code-inline">/goal resume</code>, the agent can start workflows again when your settings allow them, instead of being refused</span></li><li><span>Forking a session whose earlier turns were folded into a summary, or one forked right after its rules were updated past a compaction, now gives a fork that every client can open</span></li><li><span>Closing stdin on a <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve --no-session-log</code> host while a turn is running now sends that turn&#x27;s <code class="docs-code-inline">turn/completed</code> (cancelled) before <code class="docs-code-inline">session/closed</code>, instead of leaving the turn without a terminal</span></li><li><span>Retrying Stop while a workflow is recovering preserves its original acknowledgement</span></li><li><span>Workflow subagents that pick their own model now start in sessions launched with <code class="docs-code-inline">--yolo</code> or with approvals off</span></li></ul><h3 id="performance-6" class="docs-h docs-h3">Performance<a class="docs-anchor" href="#performance-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Resuming a session no longer re-reads every finished agent, so sessions that ran many agents open much faster</span></li><li><span>Resuming or running a session with many workflow agents spends less time refreshing the workflow control room</span></li><li><span>Resuming a session whose workflows ran many agents starts its runtime much faster</span></li></ul><h2 id="v1-4-6" class="docs-h docs-h2">1.4.6<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v1-4-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><h3 id="new-7" class="docs-h docs-h3">New<a class="docs-anchor" href="#new-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Session protocol clients can install plugins and add, update, or remove marketplaces, with change notices after each success</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> runs its own reviewer, honors a configured <code class="docs-code-inline">permissions.default_profile: &quot;:auto-review&quot;</code>, and a host with no default permission profile configured and no sandbox flags now starts new sessions on Auto-review instead of Ask me when a reviewer is available (a <code class="docs-code-inline">--disable-sandbox</code> or <code class="docs-code-inline">--sandbox-network</code> host keeps human approval; set <code class="docs-code-inline">permissions.default_profile: &quot;:ask-me&quot;</code> to keep it everywhere)</span></li><li><span>A named toolset (<code class="docs-code-inline">run.toolset</code>) can now select a server&#x27;s MCP tools with a trailing <code class="docs-code-inline">*</code>, such as <code class="docs-code-inline">mcp__docs__*</code> for every <code class="docs-code-inline">docs</code> tool or <code class="docs-code-inline">mcp__docs__search*</code> for tools whose names start with <code class="docs-code-inline">search</code></span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">task/list</code> reports the session&#x27;s running background tasks over the session protocol</span></li><li><span>Contributor mode is subscribers-only and routes each model family to its served contributor model; without an active subscription or a served contributor model the toggle stays hidden and requests go out unchanged</span></li><li><span>A <code class="docs-code-inline">PostToolBatch</code> hook now runs once after each committed tool batch with the ordered tool calls; a handler can block the batch with a reason, stop the turn, or add context that is held until the turn&#x27;s completion hook settles</span></li><li><span>A <code class="docs-code-inline">StopFailure</code> hook now runs once when a turn ends in a final model failure and receives the failure category and safe details</span></li><li><span>Choose the permission profile for a served session at start with the <code class="docs-code-inline">permissionProfile</code> member of <code class="docs-code-inline">session/start</code>; an id the host does not offer is refused before the session exists, and a session served without a signed-in provider now lists the profiles the host policy excludes as unavailable, as a signed-in host does</span></li><li><span>Managed background shell launches under Linux proxy-only networking now carry a note that ports they bind are reachable only inside that launch, naming <code class="docs-code-inline">--sandbox-network enabled</code> for serving the host</span></li><li><span>Apps using the session protocol can resume a paused workflow and replay the same receipt when retrying</span></li><li><span>Turn retry notifications now include the failing provider attempt&#x27;s details (provider system, error kind, and HTTP status) for clients that read them</span></li><li><span>Approval prompts point to <code class="docs-code-inline">/permissions</code> for changing approval defaults</span></li><li><span>Contributor mode is now on by default for subscribers, and after your first login inside the app the contributor-mode notice shows right away, before any request is sent in contributor mode; turn it off any time in <code class="docs-code-inline">/settings</code></span></li></ul><h3 id="improvements-7" class="docs-h docs-h3">Improvements<a class="docs-anchor" href="#improvements-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>The &quot;Worked for&quot; line shown after a long turn now ends with the date as well as the time, such as <code class="docs-code-inline">Worked for 2m 29s · 9:34 AM · 8/Oct</code></span></li><li><span>If you come back while a run is still going, the automatic recap now appears once that run finishes instead of being skipped</span></li><li><span>The host-network sandbox mode is now spelled <code class="docs-code-inline">unrestricted</code> (<code class="docs-code-inline">--sandbox-network unrestricted</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">network.mode: unrestricted</code>); <code class="docs-code-inline">enabled</code> still works as a deprecated silent alias</span></li><li><span>The automatic recap shown when you come back now appears after 2 minutes away (was 3) and once the session has 2 of your messages (was 3)</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">session/read</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">view/page</code> on a finished subagent&#x27;s session now return its history instead of no history or a refusal</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">PostToolBatch</code> hook feedback that ends a turn reaches the model on the next user turn, exactly once and in handler order</span></li><li><span>Pressing Esc before the model answers now gives back your message together with every message you queued after it, as one draft in the input box, images included, instead of returning only the newest queued message</span></li><li><span>Chat answers now favor diagrams drawn with text characters over raw Mermaid source</span></li><li><span>After an interruption, a Workflow task whose model and effort choice was never recorded is held with a reason instead of restarted, and recovery keeps the recorded effort even if settings changed</span></li><li><span>Agent definitions
