disclosure as cancelling a done or fixed claim, lint alone as the covering gate when a test exercises the change, or &quot;cannot run here&quot; without a failed attempt to acquire the runtime or device (install, lease, launch)</span></li><li><span>Grill uses available project checks to focus follow-up questions</span></li><li><span>The full-screen monitor view shows the command or script the watch runs, with secret values masked</span></li><li><span>The rewind picker shows turns older than the live window as read-only history</span></li><li><span>Idle composer tips can now suggest using a workflow or asking the agent to monitor a long-running task</span></li><li><span>Compaction now shows <code class="docs-code-inline">Compacting context</code> while running and <code class="docs-code-inline">Context compacted</code> when done</span></li><li><span>While working on a <code class="docs-code-inline">/goal</code>, the agent can pause its automatic follow-up turns for up to an hour while it waits on a background command or monitor, instead of checking again and again; the completion notice or your next message resumes the goal at once</span></li></ul><h3 id="fixes-11" class="docs-h docs-h3">Fixes<a class="docs-anchor" href="#fixes-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Subagent worktree git probes and cleanup dirty checks now run in the actor-confined sandbox, so hostile repo config in an agent-writable nested repo can no longer execute filter commands on the host. When the sandbox cannot be created, cleanup keeps the worktree for inspection instead of deleting it</span></li><li><span>Keep human messages that match generated summaries when replaying compacted conversations</span></li><li><span>Recover session name changes from saved checkpoints</span></li><li><span>Long sessions with a background monitor, running subagents or many open tool calls keep their live view history up to date instead of freezing</span></li><li><span>Keep previously completed Workflow indicators from reappearing when a session resumes</span></li><li><span>Ignore saved work-stop notices linked to a different session when resuming</span></li><li><span>Rejected peer messages no longer appear delivered or read</span></li><li><span>Completed message batches with invalid results show an unresolved status, consistent with message headers and groups</span></li><li><span>Lost task-stop confirmations no longer appear as a disconnected session</span></li><li><span>A subagent&#x27;s final result stays visible in its detail view instead of briefly disappearing while the view refreshes</span></li><li><span>Unstarted subagents from older sessions without saved execution state are now marked failed after a restart instead of staying scheduled forever</span></li><li><span>Prompt Hint now sees the full conversation instead of only the last turn, Away Recap has its own session cache key, and side-call model requests carry a purpose label so they are no longer mistaken for the main conversation in session records</span></li><li><span>The verify reminder&#x27;s checker now keeps its fixed <code class="docs-code-inline">high</code> level only on the Muse Spark 1.3 models at <code class="docs-code-inline">max</code> effort, the configuration that level was actually measured on. On any other model, a session at <code class="docs-code-inline">max</code> now gets a checker at its own level instead. This mattered because <code class="docs-code-inline">max</code> can be reached on models that do not offer it in the effort picker: a stored setting or an effort carried across a model switch all keep <code class="docs-code-inline">max</code>, and those sessions were being checked with a level tuned for a different model</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code> exits with the run&#x27;s own result when post-run cleanup stops responding, instead of failing a completed run</span></li><li><span>Long reasoning turns are no longer cut off by the stream idle timeout while the model is still thinking</span></li><li><span>A finished subagent now shows above the agent&#x27;s final reply in the live transcript, matching a resumed session</span></li><li><span>Restore recorded workflow completion and cancellation status when resuming a session</span></li><li><span>Stopping a watch shows one completion with its reason available in expanded details</span></li><li><span>Prevent <code class="docs-code-inline">work_stop</code> from leaving the session waiting after a subagent&#x27;s background tools stop</span></li><li><span>Keep repeated and queued messages distinct when continuing a conversation</span></li><li><span>Long sessions no longer fail every later turn with <code class="docs-code-inline">Duplicate function_call_output</code> <code class="docs-code-inline">read_file</code> are re-encoded when over 2 MiB and requests keep image payload under a budget instead of failing with HTTP 413</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">bash_input terminate</code> on a background command that carries a v2 Work ID now stops it (or returns its finished result) instead of failing with a Work Stop contract violation</span></li><li><span>Reopen saved sessions without losing their original checkpoint capture choice</span></li><li><span>Stop child agents consistently from tool requests and confirmed item or bulk actions</span></li><li><span>The <code class="docs-code-inline">/model</code> flow no longer flashes the bottom status bar between the model and reasoning-effort pickers, and the reasoning-effort picker no longer repeats a hint line on the selected row</span></li><li><span>Keep restored workflow messages in their original conversation positions after session resume</span></li><li><span>Workflow stop receipts show cancellation after the workflow stops</span></li><li><span>A turn that includes a video input no longer fails with an invalid-checkpoint error history</span></li><li><span>Pending approvals listed for a session that is not open now point at the same place in its history as the session&#x27;s saved view, on any machine</span></li><li><span>Sessions no longer exit silently at startup on terminals that never answer the cursor-position query</span></li><li><span>Preserve saved subagent stop results when retrying older long request IDs</span></li><li><span>Peer messages that cannot start a turn now show as parked until your next turn in the queue instead of looking stuck</span></li><li><span>Messages and follow-up instructions sent on later turns reach the original running subagent</span></li><li><span>A finished background result no longer stays hidden behind a stuck &quot;Working&quot; indicator when a new prompt lands as the previous turn ends</span></li><li><span>Use Up or Ctrl-P to recall a hook-blocked prompt while preserving your current draft</span></li><li><span>Oversized tool-call plugins so Esc takes you back where you started</span></li><li><span>When a checkpoint cannot be saved, the turn keeps going from the previous checkpoint instead of failing with <code class="docs-code-inline">invalid context projection checkpoint</code>; the refused checkpoint leaves nothing behind for a later read or resume to trip on</span></li><li><span>Starting a session with a chosen id no longer fails with an id conflict while the host is cleaning up an unused session directory for that id</span></li><li><span>A clean session end no longer fails on a slow disk while shutdown time remains; the final log flush now uses the whole shutdown window instead of a fixed ten seconds</span></li><li><span>Reject new managed-work batches above the session limit while preserving existing work status and controls</span></li><li><span>The monitor view&#x27;s command line keeps the rest of a command after a masked value that is glued to a commands with non-ASCII web addresses no longer crash the task view</span></li><li><span>Pasting a large block under load no longer occasionally strands its first character outside the collapsed paste placeholder</span></li><li><span>Keep subagent follow-ups working after resuming a session whose latest checkpoint was written with capture enabled, instead of failing the send with a session-read error</span></li><li><span>Setting a goal right after resume no longer fails with a goal-store custody error while the previous session-log write settles</span></li><li><span>Preserve original instructions across context compaction</span></li><li><span>Session views stay readable while the server cleans up old sessions</span></li><li><span>Resuming a session after an automatic context checkpoint keeps its todo list, so the todo reminder and later compaction summaries show the accepted items instead of an empty list</span></li><li><span>An automatic history-preserving checkpoint reply before publishing over an undelivered message, so the next turn keeps its due reminders and never compacts away text the model has not seen</span></li><li><span>Turns under the denyUnmatched approval mode no longer hang for about a minute after the answer is done</span></li><li><span>Switching sessions no longer fails when the previous session is slow to shut down</span></li><li><span>Scrolling back through an open session whose saved history stopped updating no longer shows running work as failed; loading history newer than the last save now fails with an error instead</span></li><li><span>Resuming a session after an automatic context checkpoint no longer re-records a skill you read earlier or changes the skill reminder&#x27;s view of it</span></li><li><span>Keep loaded skill instructions when trimming old tool results</span></li><li><span>Reopen a session whose newest checkpoint cannot be replayed, instead of failing the whole open</span></li><li><span>Reconcile a saved reasoning effort against the selected model instead of failing the launch when the model does not serve it</span></li><li><span>Approved peer notifications wake idle agents by default and respect explicit delivery and wake settings</span></li><li><span>Resume workflows from the session copy you opened instead of a stale source instead of acknowledging a turn and going silent; approvals parked under the profile&#x27;s prompt-unmatched ceiling become visible and answerable</span></li><li><span>Let a resumed session send a follow-up to its dormant subagent after a periodic checkpoint instead of failing the send and repeating the subagent&#x27;s earlier result</span></li><li><span>Resuming a session in the terminal app after its context was compacted delivers, exactly once, the messages from other sessions that were accepted but not yet delivered before the compaction</span></li><li><span>Work status reports when background Bash commands finish</span></li><li><span>Apps connected to <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> can show a manual compaction as running while it runs, not only after it href="#performance-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Scrolling back through a session that is not open reads its saved view instead of rereading the whole session log</span></li><li><span>Long sessions with large retained task failure messages no longer re-copy that text on every refresh</span></li><li><span>Finishing background commands and monitors no created and delivered within the same run before compaction, while keeping distinct occurrences</span></li></ul><h2 id="v1-4-1" class="docs-h docs-h2">1.4.1<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v1-4-1" docs-h3">Fixes<a class="docs-anchor" href="#fixes-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>A long session keeps its live view running when view checkpointing controls scoped to the selected session, including after recovery</span></li><li><span>Preserve each user input&#x27;s identity when restoring compacted context</span></li><li><span>Completed response setting) skips the picker from then on. <code class="docs-code-inline">/copy N</code> targets an older response</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse resume</code> and id="fixes-13" class="docs-h docs-h3">Fixes<a class="docs-anchor" href="#fixes-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> When <code class="docs-code-inline">settings.json</code> cannot be read, feedback and diagnostic upload stay off instead of turning back on over a saved opt-out</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Prompts carrying a credential in a recognized format, a token with a known vendor prefix such as <code class="docs-code-inline">sk-</code> or <code class="docs-code-inline">ghp_</code>, credentials in a URL, an <code class="docs-code-inline">Authorization:</code> header, a private key, or <code class="docs-code-inline">/login</code> with its argument, are no longer saved to prompt history or offered by recall; prompts saved before this change are unaffected</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> The local prompt-history file and its lock file are now created owner-only, so the workspace paths and session ids recorded beside each prompt are not readable by other accounts on a shared machine; a history file that already exists keeps its permissions until the store is next rewritten at the entry cap, when the owner-only replacement takes over</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Plugin agent definitions now bind the plugin package contents into their review approval, so a previously approved agent shows as modified and stays inactive until you approve it again in the plugins drawer</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Background Git status checks now run inside the sandbox, so a program named in a workspace&#x27;s Git configuration cannot change files on your machine or reach the network</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Plugin agent definitions are no longer loaded from a stale or tampered installed record; a stale record asks for a plugin refresh and a tampered one is refused as an inventory integrity failure</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> <code class="docs-code-inline">MUSE_TRANSPORT_TRACE</code> no longer prints your API bearer token when a request is retried after the credential refreshes</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Windows sandbox Root:Read now grants the sandbox group read-only access through an optional background worker; existing write, credential, token, desktop, Job and network limits remain</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> The Linux sandbox now drops every capability before running a command, so sandboxed code can no longer unmount the sandbox&#x27;s own protective mounts</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Subagents keep their admitted permission authority as a ceiling. A committed human mode change reaches running subagents at their next action in either direction, but never widens one beyond that ceiling; a request already pending keeps its captured posture</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Sapling repository commands now run inside the sandbox, so a <code class="docs-code-inline">[hooks]</code> entry in a repository&#x27;s own config can no longer execute unconfined when a workspace opens</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Limit TCP network approval rules to the exact host and port</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Redact credential-like values from provider error request and trace IDs</span></li><li><span>Keep the todo list up to date when long sessions compact older context</span></li><li><span>Active goals keep making progress after a mid-run update instead of stalling</span></li><li><span>A command that reaches a session just as it stops now fails cleanly instead of waiting forever for its reply</span></li><li><span>A video attached to a model that cannot accept video no longer breaks the session with a repeating API error; the video is skipped with an inline note and the conversation continues, including for sessions already stuck before this fix</span></li><li><span>A resumed workflow that replays its previous result now settles the workflows row instead of spinning forever</span></li><li><span>Collapsed tool headers fit narrow terminals while keeping reminder and goal outcomes visible and marking shortened text with an ellipsis</span></li><li><span>Improve recovery of queued subagent messages after interrupted session saves</span></li><li><span>Completed subagent command rows no longer reappear when switching between Main and child views</span></li><li><span>Subagent commands accept requests containing extra fields</span></li><li><span>Forking preserves user messages when the initial prompt changes after a reminder</span></li><li><span>A session started while the session-name registry is briefly locked still gets its name once the lock clears</span></li><li><span>Context compaction no longer reports you as logged out after <code class="docs-code-inline">/login</code></span></li><li><span>Skills opened with <code class="docs-code-inline">read_skill</code> now show their folder location, so helper class="docs-list"><li><span>Read-only MCP tools called in one model turn now run in parallel instead of one at a time</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse resume</code> no longer hangs for minutes at &quot;Initializing runtime&quot; on sessions whose subagent logs carry many run generations, startup now reads each subagent journal once instead of once per about a third faster and uses less memory, thanks to a new memory allocator</span></li><li><span>Resuming a session with many runs no longer re-walks the whole saved log once per run while goal progress is recovered</span></li><li><span>Long sessions resume faster when a large amount of history follows the last checkpoint</span></li><li><span>Keymap validation in <code class="docs-code-inline">tui.keymap</code> settings stays fast even when one action lists hundreds of bindings</span></li><li><span>Resuming a session with many orphaned or unreadable runs recovers sessions publish a history-preserving checkpoint every 16 MiB of retained log (tunable with <code class="docs-code-inline">context_compaction.periodic_checkpoint_bytes</code>; <code class="docs-code-inline">0</code> disables it), so a later resume reads the checkpoint plus its suffix instead of the whole log; compaction keeps publishing its own checkpoints unchanged</span></li><li><span>Task-status refreshes stay fast in long sessions with many completed tool tasks</span></li><li><span>Reduce terminal lag when refreshing child command status in sessions id="v1-2-1" class="docs-h docs-h2">1.2.1<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v1-2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><h3 id="new-13" class="docs-h docs-h3">New<a class="docs-anchor" href="#new-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Voice input is on by default on macOS: press <code class="docs-code-inline">Option+V</code> to dictate, and manage it with <code class="docs-code-inline">/voice</code></span></li><li><span>Added a <code class="docs-code-inline">/rewind</code> command that rewinds the conversation to an earlier input, same picker as double <code class="docs-code-inline">Esc</code></span></li><li><span>Pasted and dropped images get <code class="docs-code-inline">[Image #N]</code> labels the model can see, so you can ask about a specific image by number; labels and their source paths survive resume, rewind, and forks</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/mcp</code> shows a live inventory of connected MCP servers and their tools in the transcript</span></li><li><span>Added a bundled <code class="docs-code-inline">migrate</code> skill that imports your Claude Code or Codex memory notes and MCP servers into Muse Code</span></li><li><span>Set <code class="docs-code-inline">MUSE_TRANSPORT_TRACE=1</code> to print raw provider request and response lines to stderr for debugging model calls; credentials are scrubbed</span></li><li><span>Sessions can be renamed over the session protocol with <code class="docs-code-inline">session/rename</code> (with <code class="docs-code-inline">session/nameChanged</code> notifications), and <code class="docs-code-inline">session/list</code> carries display metadata, title, first user prompt, and branch</span></li><li><span>Edit-tool calls on the session protocol carry a structured diff fact, <code class="docs-code-inline">patchSummary</code> line counts plus a durable <code class="docs-code-inline">patchRef</code>: so clients can render what an edit changed</span></li><li><span>Programs driving a session can set a session-wide reasoning-effort default with <code class="docs-code-inline">session/setReasoningEffort</code>, inherited across resume and fork</span></li><li><span>Workflows now run in <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> sessions, matching what <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code> supports</span></li></ul><h3 id="improvements-14" class="docs-h docs-h3">Improvements<a class="docs-anchor" href="#improvements-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>New sessions start in the Auto-review permission profile: the same access as Ask me, with an automated reviewer deciding eligible approval requests; it falls back to asking you when the reviewer is unavailable</span></li><li><span>Permission selections are remembered and applied to new sessions</span></li><li><span>MCP tools whose server declares them read-only run without an approval prompt under on-request approvals</span></li><li><span>MCP server configs support <code class="docs-code-inline">${VAR}</code> environment interpolation, and stdio MCP servers receive <code class="docs-code-inline">MUSE_SESSION_ID</code></span></li><li><span>The MCP handshake advertises protocol version 2025-06-18 on both transports</span></li><li><span>Hook payloads include the session&#x27;s canonical <code class="docs-code-inline">model_provider</code>, so hooks can branch on the active provider</span></li><li><span>Clearer, typed guidance when a sandboxed command is denied listening on a network port</span></li><li><span>Messaging local Claude Code sessions is more robust: interrupted sends cancel cleanly, stale late replies are rejected, and peer discovery shows whether a peer supports read receipts</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">session/resume</code> runs the same startup reconciliation as a fresh launch, so work orphaned by a crash settles instead of staying stuck</span></li><li><span>Launching a subagent with an unknown agent type or an invalid task name is rejected with an explanation of what was wrong and which targets are valid</span></li><li><span>Every non-Main viewer&#x27;s footer shows <code class="docs-code-inline">Ctrl+C</code> to return, even when the view isn&#x27;t focused</span></li><li><span>Scheduled-task rows keep long prompts to a single header line, and creation receipts are one line, with detail available on expand</span></li></ul><h3 id="fixes-14" class="docs-h docs-h3">Fixes<a class="docs-anchor" href="#fixes-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> commands launched through wrappers such as <code class="docs-code-inline">env</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">setsid</code> are reviewed as the command they actually launch</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> changing the permission mode mid-session now applies to already-running tools at their next action</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> MCP tool grants in custom agent definitions are validated against the prepared toolset instead of falling back to a legacy path</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> the Unrestricted permission profile now behaves exactly like <code class="docs-code-inline">--yolo</code></span></li><li><span>Only the main and side sessions can prompt for user input; subagents no longer can</span></li><li><span>Smoother <code class="docs-code-inline">/clear</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">/new</code>: the screen no longer blanks before the new session&#x27;s first frame, keystrokes typed during the restart are kept and replayed in order, and a <code class="docs-code-inline">Ctrl-C</code> in the restart window no longer kills the app</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/clear</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">/new</code> refuse trailing text on the command line with a usage hint instead of silently discarding it</span></li><li><span>MCP servers that fail to start after <code class="docs-code-inline">/clear</code> or <code class="docs-code-inline">/new</code> now surface the failure instead of staying silent</span></li><li><span>Double <code class="docs-code-inline">Ctrl-D</code> over a pending approval opens the exit confirmation instead of force-quitting past running background work</span></li><li><span>With an approval prompt open and text in the composer, <code class="docs-code-inline">Enter</code> goes to your message instead of being swallowed by the approval panel</span></li><li><span>Each guarded call in a parallel tool batch gets its own approval prompt</span></li><li><span>Permission selections committed during a session survive resume</span></li><li><span>Pending approvals survive a headless restart instead of inheriting the predecessor&#x27;s abort</span></li><li><span>After a crash, a tool approval that was still waiting for your answer shows as unresolved on resume, never as already executed</span></li><li><span>Saving settings preserves the file&#x27;s permissions and symlinks, and no longer writes an all-default <code class="docs-code-inline">tui</code> block</span></li><li><span>MCP <code class="docs-code-inline">startup_timeout_sec</code> is honored, and slow servers that emit newline-delimited JSON are admitted</span></li><li><span>An MCP server&#x27;s <code class="docs-code-inline">required</code> flag follows the winning configuration layer</span></li><li><span>An MCP server&#x27;s <code class="docs-code-inline">cwd</code> setting now sets the stdio server&#x27;s working directory</span></li><li><span>Resuming is more reliable: resume no longer fails after compaction has pruned older history, on a session saved mid-way through parallel tool calls, on a checkpoint taken while a workflow was paused, on a checkpoint that went stale while the session kept running, or with &quot;duplicate or non-monotonic&quot; sequence errors; a run that cannot be rebuilt is set aside instead of blocking the whole session, and an empty saved session file is refused with a named reason instead of opening broken</span></li><li><span>A malformed tool call from the model no longer poisons the session: the model gets a clear error it can retry from, and sessions already saved with such a call resume cleanly</span></li><li><span>Forks and side chats are more reliable: they stay available after resuming from a checkpoint, keep messages and attachments that used to be dropped from the new branch, open on histories that previously failed with a read error, and branches created in quick succession keep their creation order</span></li><li><span>Your model and reasoning effort choices stick: forks and side chats start on the parent&#x27;s model and effort, a per-turn effort applies to that turn&#x27;s model requests, and turns the runtime starts on its own (like background-work wake-ups) use your settings instead of the startup defaults</span></li><li><span>Stopping and cancelling subagents is dependable across restarts: a stop or cancel in flight when the app closes is completed on the next launch instead of forgotten, stays in force after the agent is closed and reopened, and is not reopened by a late result from the agent&#x27;s own children; restart recovery no longer revives, duplicates, or corrupts agents it should leave alone, and closing an agent&#x27;s whole subtree no longer wakes the agents being closed</span></li><li><span>Background work reports in reliably: a live view opened before a background task produced output now fills in instead of staying blank, messages for a subagent&#x27;s own subagents reach the right agent, and a finished subagent whose session can no longer accept results settles instead of waiting forever</span></li><li><span>Workflows start and finish cleanly: an invalid workflow source is rejected before anything launches (and <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code> JSON output stays clean), a finished workflow agent with a missing or invalid report settles instead of leaving the workflow waiting, and resuming mid-workflow replays already-completed steps correctly</span></li><li><span>Workflow progress narration shows in the conversation on the default view, not only inside <code class="docs-code-inline">/workflows</code></span></li><li><span>Goals handle blocked work honestly: a goal denied by session policy ends with a clear final message naming what was blocked instead of empty output, and progress that was blocked resumes correctly when the goal continues</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code> no longer exits with an error when the process reading its stderr goes away during shutdown</span></li><li><span>Finished shell commands clean up fully: releasing a captured terminal no longer injects a stray blank line into the command&#x27;s output, and long sessions no longer accumulate runtime resources from completed commands</span></li><li><span>Session storage is more robust: listing sessions no longer intermittently fails with &quot;session index unavailable: database is locked&quot;, and a full disk no longer crashes the app before it can restore your terminal and print the session id and resume command</span></li><li><span>Pastes into <code class="docs-code-inline">!</code> shell mode stay literal, image file paths are no longer rewritten into <code class="docs-code-inline">[Image #N]</code> attachments</span></li><li><span>Long assistant replies stay within the collapsed row cap while streaming, and <code class="docs-code-inline">Ctrl+O</code> mid-stream no longer garbles the elided view</span></li><li><span>Tool rows in narrow terminals keep their expand hint instead of dropping it when the header runs out of room</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/settings</code> refreshes its rows when a side chat starts or returns, so the Reasoning effort row can&#x27;t go stale and the highlight can&#x27;t act on the wrong row</span></li><li><span>Messages parked in a side chat no longer linger in the main session&#x27;s queued-messages panel after returning</span></li><li><span>After <code class="docs-code-inline">/side</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">/status</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">/tasks</code> count only the visible session&#x27;s work instead of leaking the other session&#x27;s subagents and pending items</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/tasks</code> preview of a finished terminal shows the same status wording as its drawer row instead of &quot;no output yet&quot;</span></li><li><span>Keys pressed while the rewind loading screen is up are absorbed instead of leaking into the composer; <code class="docs-code-inline">Esc</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">Ctrl-C</code> still cancel</span></li><li><span>Resuming a session by exact id warns when its declared predecessor session is missing from the store instead of resuming silently</span></li><li><span>A freshly launched session no longer vanishes from other terminals&#x27; resume pickers until it exits</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/stop</code> always renders a verdict, a background task that never confirms now reads as a failed stop instead of leaving <code class="docs-code-inline">/stop</code> silent</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code>: <code class="docs-code-inline">session/list</code> includes sessions loaded on the answering host with fresh metadata so a new session appears immediately after <code class="docs-code-inline">session/start</code>; session recency ignores internal bookkeeping writes, so crashed old sessions no longer jump above newer work; page cursors bind to the listing that minted them, and cursors from live streaming and durable reads share one space instead of being rejected as unknown; <code class="docs-code-inline">session/setModel</code> acknowledges only after the change is durable; omitting <code class="docs-code-inline">providerId</code> on <code class="docs-code-inline">session/start</code> resolves to the host&#x27;s composed provider; a brand-new session can no longer be pruned out from under its own start; and stopping the server with SIGTERM or SIGINT winds down cleanly, closing sessions durably instead of crashing them</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code>: a rejected <code class="docs-code-inline">session/resume</code> no longer leaves a stray view subscription; resuming with a cursor delivers pending approval and user-input requests instead of an empty list; live view updates re-arm after a <code class="docs-code-inline">view/unsubscribe</code>; approval modes selected over the wire are honored for shell commands instead of being clamped; setting the model to the same provider no longer bricks a resumed session; subagent results recorded before a resume are readable again; follow-up turns spawned from a carried-forward <code class="docs-code-inline">turn/steer</code> can be interrupted and steered; the <code class="docs-code-inline">retryable</code> flag on <code class="docs-code-inline">turn/completed</code> errors reflects the provider&#x27;s real classification; reminder-spawned child tasks show their real lifecycle instead of appearing completed at spawn; and sessions started without a workspace root can still prompt via <code class="docs-code-inline">request_user_input</code> when the client supports dialogs</span></li></ul><h3 id="performance-13" class="docs-h docs-h3">Performance<a class="docs-anchor" href="#performance-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Opening or resuming a long session is dramatically faster: startup work now scales with the size of the session log rather than multiplying by the number of turns</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">item/readOutput</code> no longer scans the whole session per read, dramatically faster on long sessions</span></li><li><span>Re-attaching a live session view over <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> is now constant-time, independent of how many events streamed since load</span></li></ul><h2 id="v1-1-1" class="docs-h docs-h2">1.1.1<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v1-1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><h3 id="new-14" class="docs-h docs-h3">New<a class="docs-anchor" href="#new-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Added <code class="docs-code-inline">muse mcp login &lt;server&gt;</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">muse mcp logout &lt;server&gt;</code>: OAuth 2.1 sign-in for remote MCP servers, in the browser or headless. Tokens are kept in the auth store and refreshed automatically, a login done in another terminal is picked up without a restart, and a startup or mid-session 401 now tells you the exact <code class="docs-code-inline">muse mcp login</code> command to run. Set <code class="docs-code-inline">mcp_oauth_dynamic_client_registration: false</code> to turn off automatic client registration</span></li><li><span>Markdown links render as clickable labels in terminals that support hyperlinks, with automatic fallback (including under tmux); exported transcripts keep the full URL, and links survive redraws and scrollback</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/theme</code> gains a Terminal background row: Left/Right cycles auto, light, and dark and re-derives the picker live, a notice appears when your choice contradicts what the terminal reported, Enter saves it as <code class="docs-code-inline">tui.terminal_background</code>, and Esc reverts</span></li><li><span>The agent can check on and stop its own background work (workflows, subagents, and background commands) with the new <code class="docs-code-inline">work_status</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">work_stop</code> tools, using the same work ids it is shown</span></li><li><span>Todo reminders are on by default: the model is nudged to create and update a todo list during complex multi-step work</span></li><li><span>Two new built-in skills, on by default: one has the agent ask about an unresolved product decision before committing to it, the other keeps a focused regression test with each bug fix or behavior change</span></li><li><span>Added a bundled Three.js skill (<code class="docs-code-inline">/threejs</code>) with references for scenes, geometry, materials, lighting, textures, animation, loaders, shaders, post-processing, and interaction</span></li><li><span>Added a <code class="docs-code-inline">PostToolUseFailure</code> hook that fires when a tool call fails or crashes</span></li><li><span>After a rewind or fork, the status bar warns while tasks from the original conversation are still running, and the new branch&#x27;s transcript notes the background work that stayed behind</span></li><li><span>Press <code class="docs-code-inline">s</code> in a workflow&#x27;s detail view under <code class="docs-code-inline">/workflows</code> to save the running workflow under a name so you can run it again</span></li><li><span>Programs driving a session can declare <code class="docs-code-inline">capabilities.userInputDialogs</code> at <code class="docs-code-inline">initialize</code>; sessions whose client can show a dialog get the ask-the-user tool, and a client that opts out has such calls rejected cleanly instead of hanging</span></li><li><span>Programs driving a session can read an item&#x27;s stored tool output by reference with <code class="docs-code-inline">item/readOutput</code>, and re-attach a live view with <code class="docs-code-inline">view/subscribe</code> after <code class="docs-code-inline">view/unsubscribe</code> on a still-loaded session, replaying the gap from a cursor</span></li></ul><h3 id="improvements-15" class="docs-h docs-h3">Improvements<a class="docs-anchor" href="#improvements-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Memory, Skill, Todo, and Scope reminder child logs now default to <strong>Memory only</strong>, so a long session no longer accumulates one <code class="docs-code-inline">subagent/&lt;id&gt;/session.jsonl</code> per model step. Choose <strong>Saved</strong> under TBH Reminders → Settings to keep writing them; Goal and Verify are unchanged</span></li><li><span>A forced <code class="docs-code-inline">max</code> reasoning effort (<code class="docs-code-inline">--reasoning-effort max</code>, settings, <code class="docs-code-inline">/effort max</code>) is now sent to the model as-is on every model instead of being silently downgraded, so an unsupported value shows the provider&#x27;s error; <code class="docs-code-inline">max</code> is also accepted as a <code class="docs-code-inline">reasoningEffort</code> on <code class="docs-code-inline">turn/start</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">turn/steer</code> over the session protocol</span></li><li><span>The Scope reminder is on by default in sessions using muse-spark-1.2</span></li><li><span>Tuned the built-in instructions: the agent asks one grouped question before scaffolding when a request leaves a material product decision open, never claims a server is up without a fresh check, confirms decisive values (versions, config values, paths, counts) by a second route, surfaces degraded external causes in the deliverable itself, resolves which file a correction refers to before editing, and reports rather than refuses safety concerns about explicitly requested changes</span></li><li><span>The goal reminder no longer steers the agent toward faking, bypassing, or disabling a test to satisfy a goal; it names the honest blocker instead</span></li><li><span>Workflow scripts steer child agents to inherit the parent model unless a task clearly share one palette description, and quitting after keeping background tasks across them warns that those tasks will be stopped</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">--disable-sandbox</code> no longer prints a startup notice on its own or changes your selected permission profile; startup warns that profile filesystem and network restrictions are not enforced for direct shell commands, and <code class="docs-code-inline">/status</code> shows a Sandbox row when it was disabled at launch</span></li><li><span>Commands you run yourself with <code class="docs-code-inline">!</code> (and <code class="docs-code-inline">session/userShell</code> over <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code>) no longer trigger approval prompts, including for network access; hard policy denials still apply and stay visible</span></li><li><span>Tool calls that fail only because a path does not exist are shown quietly in a dimmed style instead of as loud errors</span></li><li><span>Tool cells with several attachments draw one continuous tree guide from the header to the last attachment, and wrapped continuations no longer land at column zero</span></li><li><span>The &quot;Worked for&quot; line also shows the local time the turn finished, e.g. <code class="docs-code-inline">Worked for 1m 01s · 10:15 AM</code></span></li><li><span>The Plan panel appears only while a run is active and hides while a prompt is waiting for your answer</span></li><li><span>When a session wakes for a peer message, the text it writes before calling a tool is folded into that tool row (expand with <code class="docs-code-inline">ctrl+o</code>) instead of a separate transcript cell</span></li><li><span>Startup notices say exactly what was trimmed: a memory truncation names the file and the limit that fired, and a skill catalog over its size limit keeps every skill&#x27;s name visible and reports how many entries were cut</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code> prints once on stderr why subagent delegation is unavailable</span></li><li><span>Spawning a subagent whose definition through completed history, oldest first</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">--worktree</code> sessions remove their Git worktree on close when it is clean and its commits are already on the default remote; unique or unproven work is kept</span></li><li><span>Sessions you open and quit before sending anything no longer linger in the resume list or on disk, including zero-turn <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> sessions whose owner process died</span></li><li><span>Removed the confusing &quot;model … not in catalog, using assumed limits&quot; notice at Effort drawer plays a gold activation animation, and the gold prompt and rail stay settled across model switches</span></li></ul><h3 id="fixes-15" class="docs-h docs-h3">Fixes<a class="docs-anchor" &lt;uuid&gt;</code>), and the export picker names its real <code class="docs-code-inline">--last</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">--session</code> flags</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec --resume</code> works for sessions created with <code class="docs-code-inline">--worktree</code>, records the crash before adopting a crashed session, and <code logs, write their control records, and recover in the right place across restarts, so their results survive a resume and are not duplicated</span></li><li><span>Subagent results no longer point at the wrong transcript when several subagents run at once; interrupting a subagent before its first model call takes effect immediately; waiting on a worktree-isolated subagent after cancelling it no longer errors; reading a subagent&#x27;s transcript works after its log crosses a checkpoint; and messages a subagent rejects are recorded with the reason</span></li><li><span>The subagent panel keeps a Finished marker that arrives out of order, shows the selected subagent&#x27;s own activity while it waits on the model, expires a finished row you parked the cursor on, names agents by label in workflow still has live child work leaves that work recoverable on the next launch, the same as after a crash</span></li><li><span>Subagents spawned by a workflow child no longer clutter the main class="docs-code-inline">/workflows</code> shows a short run id next to unnamed workflows so identical-looking rows can be told apart</span></li><li><span>Saving a named workflow no longer overwrites longer fires in sessions where the <code class="docs-code-inline">read_skill</code> tool is unavailable</span></li><li><span>One mistyped entry under <code class="docs-code-inline">skills.activation.projects</code> or <code class="docs-code-inline">hooks.state</code> no longer discards the rest of the map (a startup warning names the bad key); settings and credential writes follow a symlinked config file instead of replacing the link; and a rules directory that cannot be searched is reported by name with a remedy</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">PostCompact</code> hooks fire exactly once for background compactions adopted after a turn ends; a <code class="docs-code-inline">PostLLMCall</code> hook that keeps returning <code class="docs-code-inline">additionalContext</code> stops re-driving the turn after 8 continuations; and hook trust and enable state no longer collide between argv-style hooks whose arguments join to the same string</span></li><li><span>MCP tool calls keep their server attribution through live refreshes and after closing a rewind overlay; the per-server <code class="docs-code-inline">tool_timeout_sec</code> setting applies to tool calls, resource reads, and prompt fetches on both transports; and a server that requires an OAuth sign-in says so at startup, with HTTP 403 reported as an authentication failure instead of a generic initialization error</span></li><li><span>Interrupting a running <code class="docs-code-inline">bash</code> command returns the output it had already produced; a background command&#x27;s exit status is shown once; input sent to a non-interactive background command points at <code class="docs-code-inline">terminate</code>; starting a second <code class="docs-code-inline">!</code> command while one is running names the running command and keeps your draft; and denied <code class="docs-code-inline">!</code> commands report output truncation correctly</span></li><li><span>Search results in JSON mode return invalid-UTF-8 lines as base64 <code class="docs-code-inline">bytes</code> instead of silently rewriting them</span></li><li><span>Runaway loops that repeat the identical command with identical output are stopped even when compactions happen mid-loop</span></li><li><span>Cron jobs created during a fresh <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code> run are bound to that session; queued cron wake-ups are no longer lost when a session is resumed after a compaction; and <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> sessions expose the scheduled-task and goal tools that were advertised but never reached the model</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code> text output no longer loses the answer when a background wake starts a second run; <code class="docs-code-inline">exec</code> no longer hangs on a protected write it cannot get approved; <code class="docs-code-inline">--max-tool-output-bytes</code> rejects values below the readable floor (<code class="docs-code-inline">0</code> disables the cap); and a failed model-catalog fetch is no longer retried a second time on a cold cache</span></li><li><span>Startup no longer fails when the temp directory is unusable (it warns and continues); on Linux the startup warning about a missing system <code class="docs-code-inline">bwrap</code> is gone; and <code class="docs-code-inline">muse init</code> no longer hangs on a package manifest that is a FIFO</span></li><li><span>Meta Model API requests that fail with HTTP 402 are not retried, and retry status reads in plain words, e.g. <code class="docs-code-inline">rate limited (HTTP 429) · retrying in 60s · attempt 2/10</code>; a transient token-refresh failure during <code class="docs-code-inline">web_search</code> is reported as a connection problem instead of an authentication failure</span></li><li><span>Ctrl-B and Ctrl-D edit text when the draft is non-empty and the exit hint follows remapped keys; fast-typed or terminal-buffered text no longer arrives out of order around character-form shortcuts or Tab; cutting a large paste with Ctrl-W and yanking it back restores the content; the cursor no longer drifts after Indic spacing-mark clusters; and an image path in the middle of a sentence stays as text</span></li><li><span>Typing no longer stalls right after resuming a long session; idle sessions no longer churn CPU after a turn ends and the terminal cursor blinks again; and opening or answering an ask-question prompt no longer blanks and redraws the whole terminal</span></li><li><span>Collapsed read and search summaries always show the <code class="docs-code-inline">ctrl+o</code> hint; wrapped lines no longer tear emoji sequences or overflow the pane; narrow panes keep the state cell and timer visible for long task labels; the live-follow view for a background command uses the full pane width; an external tool&#x27;s failure details render once; and tool rows rejected for bad arguments switch to <code class="docs-code-inline">rejected</code> promptly</span></li><li><span>Run failures caused by step limits, configuration, environment, or workflow launch errors no longer carry a misleading <code class="docs-code-inline">model failed</code> prefix; the context-usage notice no longer reports almost nothing remaining on an implausible token count; and the notice shown when resuming a session that did not shut down cleanly no longer tells you to run <code class="docs-code-inline">reset</code></span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">--worktree</code> sessions no longer fail intermittently when several sessions create worktrees in the same repository at once, and resuming one no longer hits a worktree collision after an earlier removal was interrupted</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse export --out</code> writes to a temporary sibling and renames it into place, so a failed export never truncates an existing file</span></li><li><span>Pending approvals no longer flash into the approval list while the automated reviewer is still deciding</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">@muse-code/sdk</code> bundles its protocol type declarations, so consumers typecheck with <code class="docs-code-inline">skipLibCheck</code> off; <code class="docs-code-inline">Item.turnId</code> is typed as nullable to match what the server sends</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code>: protected-write approvals wait for the subscribed client&#x27;s <code class="docs-code-inline">approval/decide</code> instead of aborting right after prompting; <code class="docs-code-inline">session/resume</code> re-issues pending approval and user-input requests so a reconnecting client can answer them after a crash; a resume with a cursor no longer lets a live event reach the client before the replayed suffix; and views restored after a restart match the live view when a reply was still streaming at checkpoint time</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code>: <code class="docs-code-inline">session/list</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">session/read</code>, and <code class="docs-code-inline">session/resume</code> report <code class="docs-code-inline">running</code> and the active <code class="docs-code-inline">turnId</code> while a turn is in flight; a session whose cached view history is unreadable reports history as unavailable instead of failing every read; failed, cancelled, and timed-out tool calls include the tool&#x27;s final output; <code class="docs-code-inline">session/start</code> ignores unknown keys inside <code class="docs-code-inline">config</code> instead of failing; rejected <code class="docs-code-inline">userShell</code> commands are settled durably so an identical retry gets the original answer; and a queued follow-up left stranded when the connection closed mid-admission is no longer executed on the next load</span></li><li><span>Scheduled (cron) deliveries run as one bounded turn: the end-of-turn goal reminder no longer fires on a scheduled run, which had kept a single delivery looping through phantom ticks every few seconds</span></li><li><span>A <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> host that started logged out now picks up a later device-code login on the next session start, resume, or fork instead of answering &quot;auth required&quot; until the host restarts</span></li></ul><h3 id="performance-14" class="docs-h docs-h3">Performance<a class="docs-anchor" href="#performance-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">view/page</code> on long sessions is dramatically faster over <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code>: page reads are linear in session size and repeat pages on a loaded session are served from cache</span></li><li><span>Faster startup and resume: multi-megabyte checkpoint lines are read in linear time, session-index housekeeping and crash-recovery scans run after the prompt is ready, the trust store is read once per launch, a turn submitted into a resumed session no longer replays history older than the last compaction, and <code class="docs-code-inline">session/resume</code> over <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> loads from the latest checkpoint instead of replaying the whole log</span></li><li><span>Rewind evaluates and applies from an in-memory window of the current conversation (back to the latest compaction checkpoint) instead of re-reading the session log, so the picker opens faster in long sessions</span></li></ul><h2 id="v1-0-x" class="docs-h docs-h2">1.0.x<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v1-0-x" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Also delivered in 1.0.x patches: the <code class="docs-code-inline">tui.terminal_background</code> setting (<code class="docs-code-inline">auto</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">light</code>, or <code class="docs-code-inline">dark</code>); <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> sessions expose the same <code class="docs-code-inline">bash</code> tools as <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">model/list</code> lists only the models a session can route to, <code class="docs-code-inline">session/resume</code> from a cursor delivers the retained events after it, an oversized <code class="docs-code-inline">session/start</code> workspace path is refused and <code class="docs-code-inline">session/list</code> pages large listings, <code class="docs-code-inline">initialize</code> rejects a malformed <code class="docs-code-inline">clientInfo.name</code>, and <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> exits with code 3 when settings or credentials cannot be loaded; forking carries compacted permission state into the fork; forked and side sessions show their real creation time instead of 1970; web search reads compressed responses; logging out clears the cached feature configuration; the skill reminder is active again in default <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code> runs and no longer repeats its loaded notice; the blocking verify reminder header reads &quot;Double checking&quot;; resume tolerates a blank line in the session log; checkpoint and explicit saves no longer stall behind background flushing; memory writes survive a stale temp file left by a crash; subagent results and goal reminders arrive as developer context; the search tool routes filename lookups to <code class="docs-code-inline">glob</code>; Esc exits input-history browsing and restores your draft; <code class="docs-code-inline">/resume</code> inside the app shows startup progress instead of a frozen screen; the <code class="docs-code-inline">/tasks</code> drawer lists only the visible session&#x27;s tasks; a retried <code class="docs-code-inline">turn/interrupt</code> after a restart no longer records a duplicate rejection; and two security fixes: on-request approval mode requires approval when shell arguments cannot be fully parsed, and provider error messages no longer include the credential that failed.</p><h2 id="v0-2-1" class="docs-h docs-h2">0.2.1<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v0-2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><h3 id="new-15" class="docs-h docs-h3">New<a class="docs-anchor" href="#new-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Rewind the conversation with a double Esc: pick an earlier point, confirm before anything is undone, and only safe rewind points are offered</span></li><li><span>Automatic approval pre-screening: a model-based reviewer clears tool requests it judges safe, so you see fewer prompts. Anything it doesn&#x27;t clear still comes to you, and it can be disabled</span></li><li><span>When the sandbox blocks a command, the agent can ask for a one-time approval to run that exact command outside it</span></li><li><span>Added a &quot;Review plan&quot; action to step through long plans that overflow the panel</span></li><li><span>Added <code class="docs-code-inline">muse config</code> to validate enterprise-managed configuration documents</span></li><li><span>Added a built-in skill for setting up isolated Python environments</span></li><li><span>Added a built-in skill for handing off and verifying browser apps the agent builds</span></li><li><span>Hook commands now receive a selected set of environment variables</span></li><li><span>The input box can show a short contextual hint after a turn finishes</span></li></ul><h3 id="improvements-16" class="docs-h docs-h3">Improvements<a class="docs-anchor" href="#improvements-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Approval dialogs wait for a pause in your typing before appearing, so they stop stealing keystrokes mid-sentence</span></li><li><span>Permission decisions are retained in the session log and restored on resume</span></li><li><span>The resume picker surfaces sessions that were previously hidden</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">--model</code> accepts any model id; unknown ids use sensible assumed metadata instead of being rejected</span></li><li><span>Settings accept the standard <code class="docs-code-inline">mcpServers</code> key, matching the common ecosystem format</span></li><li><span>MCP configuration across multiple files and scopes merges consistently</span></li><li><span>Clearer diagnostics when an MCP server fails to start, reported once instead of pinned in the interface</span></li><li><span>Optional MCP servers that fail at startup no longer spam the transcript</span></li><li><span>You can see which of your hooks are running in the live activity area</span></li><li><span>Messages sent as a turn finishes are delivered together in one follow-up turn</span></li><li><span>Text typed as part of a rewind is kept and restored</span></li><li><span>The agent can ask longer questions, up to 500 characters</span></li><li><span>The Write tool flags when a new file nearly duplicates an existing one</span></li><li><span>Sessions at <code class="docs-code-inline">ultra</code> reasoning effort default to maximum parallel-agent capacity unless you set a limit</span></li><li><span>Session export stitches in subagent transcripts that finish independently</span></li><li><span>Redesigned <code class="docs-code-inline">/status</code> as a cleaner summary card</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/usage</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">/models</code> label costs explicitly as USD</span></li><li><span>Skill slash commands are highlighted while you type</span></li><li><span>Tables stay narrow enough to read in a terminal</span></li><li><span>The bundled plan skill researches sources first and presents the plan for review before starting work</span></li><li><span>Rewrote the built-in plan, doctor, and source-control skills with clearer guidance</span></li><li><span>The design skill reliably engages before the assistant writes visual web frontend code</span></li><li><span>Within a session, the agent remembers which skills it already read and avoids redundant re-reads</span></li><li><span>Skills with aliases appear once under their canonical name</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">skills import --from</code> errors now list the accepted values</span></li></ul><h3 id="fixes-16" class="docs-h docs-h3">Fixes<a class="docs-anchor" href="#fixes-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> a malicious repository&#x27;s git configuration can no longer run arbitrary commands</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> git commands on your repos ignore repo-configured hooks, so a malicious repo can&#x27;t run code through them</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> skill text containing hidden terminal-control characters is rejected, preventing display spoofing</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> Linux sandboxed commands can no longer reach host services through Unix-domain sockets</span></li><li><span><strong>Security:</strong> a folder carrying both Mercurial and Sapling metadata is no longer probed for repository status</span></li><li><span>Fixed a crash when resuming a session whose background agent run couldn&#x27;t be re-read</span></li><li><span>Fixed a panic when piping output into commands such as <code class="docs-code-inline">head</code></span></li><li><span>Fixed a crash on non-UTF-8 command-line arguments</span></li><li><span>Partial model responses cut off mid-stream are kept and marked incomplete instead of lost</span></li><li><span>Model calls fail fast with a clear status when the network is down, instead of hanging through silent retries</span></li><li><span>The working indicator and retry countdown stay visible when a response drops mid-stream</span></li><li><span>Streamed answer text no longer appears in the wrong place before the response type is known</span></li><li><span>HTTP and HTTPS proxy environment variables are respected for all network traffic</span></li><li><span>Keystrokes are no longer lost while an approval decision is submitting</span></li><li><span>Multi-line pasted text stays together, including in terminals without bracketed-paste support</span></li><li><span>Fixed shifted keys being misread in older VS Code terminals</span></li><li><span>Prompts typed in quick succession while a run starts are accepted instead of dropped</span></li><li><span>Prompts appear in the transcript as soon as you submit them, even while the run is still starting</span></li><li><span>Ctrl-C withdraws queued messages that hadn&#x27;t started yet</span></li><li><span>A steering message you already sent is no longer lost when you retract the turn</span></li><li><span>Retracting a turn just after a steering message went through no longer freezes the interface</span></li><li><span>Prompts entered when forking a session run in the forked session, not the original</span></li><li><span>Esc interrupts the end-of-turn reminder wait instead of appearing to hang</span></li><li><span>Tools no longer time out while waiting for you to answer an approval prompt</span></li><li><span>Resume restores permission prompts that were still awaiting an answer</span></li><li><span>Resumed sessions keep the approval mode you chose</span></li><li><span>Permission prompts stay visible when the side panel refreshes</span></li><li><span>Denying a network permission request now tells the agent and shows in the transcript</span></li><li><span>The automatic permission reviewer is more predictable, with consistent verdicts, retry caps, and timeouts</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/compact</code> compacts the session&#x27;s real working set, including after forks and side chats</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/compact</code> runs in the background instead of blocking the session</span></li><li><span>Branching into a side chat after a restart no longer breaks conversation history</span></li><li><span>Resume replays subagent activity recorded in the parent session log, with the original identity</span></li><li><span>Resumed sessions keep subagent lifecycle events in their original order</span></li><li><span>Output from background subagents started before a resume is replayed instead of disappearing</span></li><li><span>Subagent results that finished before you pressed Esc are preserved instead of disappearing with the cancelled turn</span></li><li><span>Long-running background subagents reliably deliver their final answer</span></li><li><span>Input submitted just before the app stops is no longer stranded on resume</span></li><li><span>Resume no longer writes checkpoints from a half-replayed log, or breaks on expected gaps in the checkpoint log</span></li><li><span>Resume no longer risks adopting the wrong <code class="docs-code-inline">/compact</code> result during recovery</span></li><li><span>Manual <code class="docs-code-inline">/compact</code> runs are recorded durably and survive restarts</span></li><li><span>A log truncated mid-write no longer restores a partially written permission record</span></li><li><span>Session goals are restored with working controls after a kill and resume, and usage totals stay correct when a goal is replaced</span></li><li><span>Resumed session goals restore their usage totals instead of failing to resume</span></li><li><span>Session goals pause when successive turns stop making progress, instead of looping indefinitely</span></li><li><span>Exported sessions keep the full record of permission prompts and decisions</span></li><li><span>Sessions get a proper end record on normal exit, keeping history and resume listings accurate</span></li><li><span>Closing or losing your terminal is no longer misreported as a crash</span></li><li><span>Starting two sessions at the same moment no longer fails to open the local session store on a first run</span></li><li><span>Starting from a missing or unreadable folder fails immediately with a clear error</span></li><li><span>A prompt passed at startup is no longer occasionally captured as blank</span></li><li><span>Fixed a race at run start that could leave the session in a confused launch state</span></li><li><span>Headless runs pass your prompt text through unmodified by default</span></li><li><span>A <code class="docs-code-inline">!</code> shell command whose process dies unexpectedly settles cleanly instead of leaving the session stuck</span></li><li><span>Background processes are cleaned up more reliably when a session exits</span></li><li><span>The agent gets correct guidance for backgrounding commands from the shell tool on macOS</span></li><li><span>Stopping a background task no longer hangs when two stop requests race</span></li><li><span>Background reminder checks are tied to their own run, so no activity lingers after it ends</span></li><li><span>Headless runs no longer hang after finishing because an older reminder task is still open</span></li><li><span>Background command and task ids are globally unique and time-ordered</span></li><li><span>Scheduled tasks with a timezone problem warn once instead of every tick</span></li><li><span>A corrupt scheduled-task database now warns at startup and identifies where the quarantined data was retained</span></li><li><span>A failed subagent launch no longer permanently consumes a capacity slot</span></li><li><span>Subagents that finish without a result show a proper final state</span></li><li><span>Notes typed in a subagent&#x27;s view reach the running subagent</span></li><li><span>Subagent worktrees whose ownership can&#x27;t be proven after a crash are quarantined instead of wrongly cleaned up</span></li><li><span>Status lines for cancelled and waiting agents show the agent name instead of a raw UUID</span></li><li><span>Messages with pasted images sent while the agent is busy arrive in order</span></li><li><span>Pasting an image alongside a pending rewind routes correctly</span></li><li><span>Hook output starting with a UTF-8 BOM has its allow or deny decision honored</span></li><li><span>Project hooks take effect as soon as you trust a folder, without a restart</span></li><li><span>Hooks triggered by <code class="docs-code-inline">!</code> shell commands are durably recorded and survive resume and export</span></li><li><span>Structured JSON output from file hooks is preserved instead of flattened</span></li><li><span>Rejected hook output produces a bounded, readable diagnostic</span></li><li><span>Shell approval prompts keep the command&#x27;s original line breaks</span></li><li><span>Invalid todo-list tool arguments produce a proper structured error</span></li><li><span>A malformed skill on or off value in settings is ignored gracefully instead of breaking loading</span></li><li><span>Prompt hints only suggest commands that exist in your session</span></li><li><span>A symlinked user config directory no longer breaks loading of project and built-in agent definitions</span></li><li><span>Fixed a settings file lock held longer than needed, which could block later writes</span></li><li><span>Ctrl-L clears the screen without redraw artifacts</span></li><li><span><code class="docs-code-inline">/help</code> shows the full shortcut list in an 80×24 terminal</span></li><li><span>Fixed a wildly wrong elapsed time in the activity row after reattaching to a session</span></li><li><span>The task panel no longer glitches while old checkpoints are retired</span></li><li><span>The <code class="docs-code-inline">ultra</code> reasoning-effort display and activation animation no longer pop, flicker, or dim</span></li><li><span>On Linux, the command sandbox is selected once at startup so behavior stays consistent for the session</span></li><li><span>The built-in doctor skill&#x27;s session-evidence collection and redaction work correctly again</span></li></ul><h3 id="performance-15" class="docs-h docs-h3">Performance<a class="docs-anchor" href="#performance-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Faster startup with a large skill catalog, and an accurate count of skills dropped from the catalog</span></li><li><span>Git operations for isolated subagent worktrees no longer block the agent runtime</span></li></ul><h2 id="v0-1-x" class="docs-h docs-h2">0.1.x<a class="docs-anchor" href="#v0-1-x" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Also delivered in 0.1.x patches: attaching the session recording when reporting a bug as well as a bad result; correct truecolor detection for Ghostty over SSH; reliable replay of terminal command output class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Write a script for this repository that tells me what changed in Muse Code since the version I run. Read the installed version from `muse --version`, fetch https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/changelog.md, parse it into releases with their New, Improvements, Fixes and Performance sections, and print every change newer than mine, security fixes first. Exit nonzero when the fetch or the parse fails.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Changelog&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/changelog.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/changelog

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- Each release is a `## &lt;version&gt;` heading, newest first, with `### New`, `### Improvements`, `### Fixes` and `### Performance` sections of `- ` bullets.
- Some releases (1.0.x, 0.1.x) are one paragraph of patch notes instead of sections, and 0.1.0 is a single bullet.
- x in a heading (1.0.x) matches any number. Stop at the first heading at or below the installed version: 1.0.3 stops at 1.0.x, and a version newer than the page has nothing to print.
- Security fixes start with `**Security:**`.
- The page gives no release dates. Its anchors are v plus the version with dots as hyphens (#v1-4-13).

Starter code (Python)
import re
import subprocess
import sys

import requests

out = subprocess.run([&quot;muse&quot;, &quot;--version&quot;], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
found = re.search(r&quot;\d+\.\d+\.\d+&quot;, out)
if not found:
    sys.exit(f&quot;Can&#x27;t read a version from {out!r}&quot;)
mine = [int(n) for n in found.group(0).split(&quot;.&quot;)]

def at_or_below(heading):
    &quot;&quot;&quot;The installed version or older; x matches any number (1.0.x).&quot;&quot;&quot;
    for part, own in zip(heading.split(&quot;.&quot;), mine):
        if part == &quot;x&quot;:
            return True
        if int(part) != own:
            return int(part) &lt; own
    return True

md = requests.get(&quot;https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/changelog.md&quot;, timeout=30)
md.raise_for_status()

changes, version, kind, releases = [], None, &quot;Notes&quot;, 0
for line in md.text.splitlines():
    if line.startswith(&quot;## &quot;):
        releases += 1
        heading = line[3:].split()[0]
        if at_or_below(heading):
            break
        version, kind = heading, &quot;Notes&quot;
    elif version and line.startswith(&quot;### &quot;):
        kind = line[4:].strip()
    elif version and line.strip():
        changes.append((version, kind, line.removeprefix(&quot;- &quot;).strip()))
if not releases:
    sys.exit(&quot;No releases found: has the page&#x27;s format changed?&quot;)
if not changes:
    print(f&quot;Up to date: nothing newer than {found.group(0)}.&quot;)
for v, k, text in sorted(changes, key=lambda c: not c[2].startswith(&quot;**Security&quot;)):
    print(f&quot;{v} [{k}] {text}&quot;)

Done when
- Given 1.4.10 it prints the 1.4.11, 1.4.12 and 1.4.13 changes and nothing older; given 1.0.3 it stops at 1.0.x; given 1.4.14 it says it&#x27;s up to date.
- Security fixes come first, and an unreachable URL exits nonzero.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">3,606<!-- --> characters</span><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-primary docs-btn-sm"><svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy prompt</span></button></div></div></div><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" title="Copy this page as Markdown"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy page</span></button><a class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" href="https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/changelog" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M14 4h6v6 M20 4l-9 9 M18 14v4.5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-1.5 1.5h-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 4 18.5v-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 5.5 6H10"></path></svg><span>View on dev.meta.ai</span><span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a><p class="docs-rail-note">Independent concept built on Meta&#x27;s Model API.
